verses.text: Blessed is the one who doesn’t follow the advice of the wicked, stand in the path of sinners, or sit with those who mock.
Instead, they delight in the LORD’s instruction and think about it day and night.
They’re like a tree planted by streams of water, bearing fruit in season, with leaves that never wither. Whatever they do prospers.
The wicked are nothing like that. They’re like chaff that the wind blows away.
So the wicked won’t stand when judgment comes, and sinners won’t stand among those who do what is right.
The LORD knows the path of the righteous, but the path of the wicked leads to ruin.
Why are the nations raging? Why are the peoples making plans that will come to nothing?
The kings of the earth take their stand, and the rulers plot together against the LORD and his Anointed One. They say,
“Let’s break their chains and throw off their ropes.”
The one enthroned in heaven laughs. The Lord makes fun of them.
Then he speaks to them in anger and terrifies them with his wrath:
“I’ve already set my King on Zion, my holy hill.”
I’ll tell you what the LORD declared to me: “You are my son. Today I have become your father.
Ask me, and I’ll give you the nations as your inheritance and the far ends of the earth as your own.
You’ll break them with an iron rod and smash them like a clay pot.”
So wise up, you kings. Take this warning, you judges of the earth.
Serve the LORD with reverence and rejoice with trembling.
Honor the Son sincerely, or his anger may flare up and you’ll perish along the way. Blessed are all who take refuge in him.
A psalm by David, when he fled from his son Absalom. LORD, my enemies keep growing in number! So many are rising up against me.
So many say about me, “God won’t help him.” Selah.
But you, LORD, are a shield around me. You are my glory, the one who lifts my head.
I cry aloud to the LORD, and he answers me from his holy hill. Selah.
I lay down and slept. I woke up again because the LORD keeps me safe.
I won’t be afraid, even if tens of thousands surround me on every side.
Rise up, LORD! Save me, my God! You’ve struck all my enemies in the face and broken the teeth of the wicked.
Salvation belongs to the LORD. May your blessing rest on your people. Selah.
For the music director, with stringed instruments. A psalm by David. Answer me when I call, God who upholds my cause. Give me room to breathe in my distress. Have mercy and hear my prayer.
People, how long will you turn my honor into shame? How long will you love empty things and chase lies? Selah.
Know that the LORD has set apart the faithful for himself. The LORD hears when I call to him.
Tremble with awe and don’t sin. When you lie down, search your heart and be still. Selah.
Offer sacrifices that are right, and put your trust in the LORD.
Many ask, “Who will show us anything good?” LORD, let the light of your face shine on us.
You’ve given me more joy than they have when their grain and fresh wine are plentiful.
I’ll lie down and sleep in peace, because you alone, LORD, keep me safe.
For the music director, with flutes. A psalm by David. Hear my words, LORD. Pay attention to what weighs on my mind.
Listen to my cry for help, my King and my God, because I’m praying to you.
LORD, you’ll hear my voice in the morning. I’ll lay my requests before you at dawn and watch for your answer.
You take no pleasure in wickedness. Evil can’t live with you.
The arrogant can’t stand in your presence. You hate everyone who does wrong.
You destroy those who tell lies. The LORD detests those who are bloodthirsty and deceitful.
But because of your abundant faithful love, I can enter your house. I’ll bow toward your holy temple in reverence for you.
LORD, guide me in your righteousness with enemies around me. Make your path straight before me.
Nothing they say can be trusted. Their hearts plot ruin. Their throats are open graves, and their tongues are full of flattery.
Hold them guilty, God. Let their own schemes bring them down. Drive them out for all their wrongs, because they’ve rebelled against you.
But let everyone who takes refuge in you rejoice. Let them always shout for joy because you protect them. Let those who love your name find joy in you.
You bless those who do what is right, LORD. You surround them with your favor like a shield.
For the music director, with stringed instruments, on the eight-stringed lyre. A psalm by David. LORD, don’t rebuke me in your anger or discipline me in your wrath.
Have mercy on me, LORD, because I’m weak. Heal me, LORD, because my bones are shaking.
I’m shaken to my core. LORD, how long will this go on?
Turn back to me, LORD. Rescue me. Save me because of your faithful love.
In death no one remembers you. Who can thank you from Sheol?
I’m worn out from groaning. Every night my tears flood my bed and soak the place where I lie.
My eyes grow weak with grief. They wear out because of all my enemies.
Get away from me, all you who do evil, because the LORD has heard me weeping.
The LORD has heard my plea. The LORD accepts my prayer.
May all my enemies be ashamed and shaken. They’ll turn back, disgraced in an instant.
A meditation by David, sung to the LORD about what Cush the Benjaminite said. LORD my God, I take refuge in you. Save me from everyone chasing me. Rescue me
before they tear me apart like a lion, ripping me to pieces with no one to save me.
LORD my God, if I’ve done what they say, if my hands are guilty,
if I’ve done harm to someone who was at peace with me or robbed someone who opposed me for no reason,
then let my enemy chase me down and catch me. Let him trample my life into the ground and leave my honor in the dust. Selah.
Rise up in anger, LORD. Stand against the fury of my enemies. Wake up and help me. You’ve called for judgment.
Let the assembled peoples gather around you. Rule over them from on high.
The LORD judges the peoples. Judge me, LORD, according to my righteousness and the integrity in me.
Put an end to the evil the wicked are doing, and give the righteous a firm footing. You are the righteous God who searches hearts and minds.
God is my shield. He saves people whose hearts are honest.
God is a righteous judge, a God who feels indignation every day.
If a person refuses to turn back, God sharpens his sword. He has already bent his bow and strung it.
He’s prepared his deadly weapons and made his flaming arrows ready.
Look at the one who labors to do evil. They conceive trouble and give birth to lies.
They dig a hole and fall into the very pit they made.
The trouble they cause comes back on their own head. Their violence lands on them.
I’ll thank the LORD for his righteousness and sing praise to the name of the LORD Most High.
For the music director, on an instrument from Gath. A psalm by David. LORD, our Lord, how majestic is your name across the whole earth! You’ve set your glory above the heavens.
From the lips of children and infants you’ve built a strong defense against your foes, to silence the enemy and the avenger.
When I look at your heavens, the work of your fingers, at the moon and stars you set in place,
what are human beings that you think of them, or mortals that you care for them?
Yet you made them a little lower than the angels and crowned them with glory and honor.
You put them in charge of what your hands made. You placed everything under their feet:
all the sheep and cattle, and even the wild animals,
the birds in the sky, the fish in the sea, and everything that travels the paths of the seas.
LORD, our Lord, how majestic is your name across the whole earth!
For the music director, to the tune of “The Death of the Son.” A psalm by David. I’ll thank the LORD with my whole heart. I’ll tell about all the wonders you’ve done.
I’ll be glad and rejoice in you. I’ll sing praises to your name, Most High.
When my enemies turn back, they stumble and perish in your presence.
You’ve upheld my just cause. You sit on your throne and judge with righteousness.
You’ve rebuked the nations and destroyed the wicked. You’ve erased their name forever.
The enemy has fallen into ruin without end. Even the memory of the cities you overthrew is gone.
But the LORD reigns forever. He’s set up his throne for judgment.
He’ll judge the world with righteousness and give the peoples a fair judgment.
The LORD is a fortress for the oppressed, a place of safety in times of trouble.
Those who know your name trust you, because you, LORD, have never abandoned those who seek you.
Sing praises to the LORD, who lives in Zion. Tell the peoples what he’s done.
The one who avenges bloodshed remembers those who suffer. He never forgets their cries.
Have mercy on me, LORD. See how those who hate me make me suffer. Lift me away from the gates of death,
so I can tell of all your praises and rejoice in your rescue at the gates of the daughter of Zion.
The nations have sunk into the pit they dug. Their own feet are caught in the net they hid.
The LORD has made himself known by bringing judgment. The wicked are caught by what their own hands have done. Meditation. Selah.
The wicked will go down to Sheol, along with every nation that forgets God.
The needy won’t be forgotten forever, and the hope of the poor won’t always be lost.
Rise up, LORD! Don’t let human power win. Bring the nations before you for judgment.
Make them tremble, LORD. Let the nations know they’re only human. Selah.
Why do you stand so far away, LORD? Why do you hide when trouble comes?
In their arrogance the wicked hunt down the weak. Let them get caught in the schemes they devise.
The wicked boast about what they crave. They bless the greedy and speak against the LORD.
The wicked carry themselves with pride. There’s no room for God in their thoughts.
Everything they do seems to prosper. They’re arrogant and keep your laws out of sight. They sneer at all their enemies.
They tell themselves, “Nothing will shake me. Trouble won’t touch me for generations.”
Their mouths are full of curses, lies, and threats. Trouble and evil are under their tongues.
They lie in wait near villages and murder innocent people from hiding. They keep a secret watch on those who can’t defend themselves.
They hide like a lion waiting to pounce. They lie in wait for the helpless and catch them by pulling them into their nets.
The helpless are crushed. They collapse and fall under the weight of their attackers.
The wicked tell themselves, “God has forgotten. He’s turned away. He’ll never see it.”
Rise up, LORD! Lift up your hand, God! Remember those who can’t defend themselves.
Why do the wicked speak against God and tell themselves, “He’ll never hold me to account”?
But you do see their trouble and grief, and you take it into your own hands. You help the victim and the fatherless.
Break the power of the wicked. Call evildoers to account until no wickedness is left to uncover.
The LORD is King forever and ever! The nations will vanish from his land.
LORD, you hear what the humble long for. You steady their hearts and listen to them,
to give justice to the fatherless and the oppressed, so mere mortals can terrorize them no more.
For the music director. By David. I take refuge in the LORD. How can you tell me, “Fly to your mountain like a bird”?
Look, the wicked are bending their bows and setting arrows on the strings, ready to shoot from the dark at people whose hearts are right.
When the foundations are torn down, what can the righteous do?
The LORD is in his holy temple. His throne is in heaven. He watches closely and examines all people.
The LORD examines the righteous, and he hates the wicked and those who love violence.
He’ll rain burning coals on the wicked. Fire, sulfur, and scorching wind will fill their cup.
The LORD is righteous, and he loves what is right. The upright will see his face.
For the music director, on an eight-stringed lyre. A psalm of David. Help, LORD! The godly are gone, and faithful people are disappearing.
Everyone lies to their neighbor. They flatter with their lips while hiding what’s in their hearts.
May the LORD silence every flattering lip and every boasting tongue,
all those who say, “Our words will put us on top. Our lips are our own. Who can tell us what to do?”
“The weak are oppressed and the needy are groaning, so I’ll rise up now,” says the LORD. “I’ll keep them safe from those who speak against them.”
The LORD’s words are flawless, like silver refined in a clay furnace and purified seven times.
You’ll protect them, LORD, and keep them safe from this generation forever.
The wicked strut everywhere when people praise what is vile.
For the music director. A psalm by David. How long, LORD? Will you forget me forever? How long will you hide your face from me?
How long must I wrestle with my thoughts and carry sorrow in my heart every day? How long will my enemy have the upper hand?
Look at me and answer, LORD my God. Put light back in my eyes, or I’ll fall asleep in death.
Then my enemy will say, “I beat him,” and those who oppose me will celebrate my fall.
But I trust your faithful love. My heart rejoices because you save me.
I’ll sing to the LORD because he’s been good to me.
For the music director. By David. The fool says in their heart, “There is no God.” People are corrupt and do terrible things. No one does good.
The LORD looks down from heaven on humanity to see if anyone understands and seeks God.
Everyone has turned away. Together they’ve become corrupt. No one does good. No one at all.
Don’t any of these evildoers understand? They devour my people as casually as they eat bread, and they never call on the LORD.
But there they are, terrified, because God is with those who do what is right.
You try to ruin the plans of the poor, but the LORD is their refuge.
If only Israel’s rescue would come from Zion! When the LORD restores his people’s fortunes, Jacob will rejoice and Israel will be glad.
A psalm by David. LORD, who may stay in your sanctuary? Who may live on your holy hill?
Those who live with integrity, do what is right, and speak the truth from the heart.
They don’t slander anyone, harm their friends, or insult their neighbors.
They look down on those who act disgracefully and honor those who fear the LORD. They keep their promises even when it costs them.
They lend money without charging interest and never take a bribe to harm the innocent. Whoever lives this way will never be shaken.
A poem by David. Keep me safe, God, because I take refuge in you.
I’ve said to the LORD from my soul, “You are my Lord. Every good thing I have comes from you.”
The holy people in the land are the ones I admire. I find great joy in them.
Those who bring gifts to another god will only add to their sorrows. I won’t pour out their offerings of blood or even speak the names of those gods.
The LORD has given me my portion and filled my cup. You keep what’s mine secure.
The boundary lines have fallen in pleasant places for me. I’ve received a good inheritance.
I’ll bless the LORD for guiding me. Even at night my heart teaches me.
I keep the LORD before me at all times. Because he’s at my right hand, I won’t be shaken.
So my heart is glad, my tongue sings for joy, and my body rests secure.
You won’t abandon me to Sheol. You won’t let your holy one see decay.
You’ll show me the path of life. In your presence there is fullness of joy. At your right hand there is delight forever.
A prayer by David. LORD, hear my just plea. Listen to my prayer. There’s no deceit on my lips.
Let my verdict come from you. Look on what is fair.
You’ve tested my heart and come to me in the night. You’ve examined me and found nothing. I’ve made up my mind to keep my mouth from wrongdoing.
Whatever others do, I’ve followed what you said and stayed away from the paths of violent people.
I’ve kept to your paths. My feet haven’t slipped.
I call on you, God, because you’ll answer me. Turn your ear toward me and hear what I say.
Show your wonderful faithful love. With your right hand you save those who take refuge in you from their enemies.
Guard me like the apple of your eye. Hide me in the shadow of your wings,
away from the wicked who oppress me, from the deadly enemies who surround me.
They’ve shut their hearts to pity, and they talk with pride.
They’ve tracked us down and now surround us, watching for a chance to throw us to the ground.
My enemy is like a lion hungry for prey, like a young lion lurking in a hiding place.
Rise up, LORD! Confront him and bring him down. Rescue me from the wicked with your sword.
Save me by your hand, LORD, from people whose share is in this life. You fill the bellies of those you cherish. Their children have plenty, and they leave wealth for their children.
As for me, I’ll see your face in righteousness. When I wake, seeing you will be enough.
For the music director. David, the LORD’s servant, sang this song to the LORD when the LORD rescued him from all his enemies and from Saul. He said, “I love you, LORD, my strength.”
The LORD is my rock, my fortress, and my rescuer. My God is the rock where I take refuge, my shield, my saving horn, and my stronghold.
I call to the LORD, who deserves praise, and he saves me from my enemies.
The ropes of death closed around me, and floods of wickedness terrified me.
The ropes of Sheol wrapped around me. Death’s traps lay in my path.
In my distress I called to the LORD and cried out to my God. He heard me from his temple. My cry reached his ears.
The earth shook and trembled. The foundations of the mountains shook because he was angry.
Smoke rose from his nostrils. A fire that devours came from his mouth and set coals ablaze.
He bent the heavens down and came to earth, with thick darkness under his feet.
He rode on a cherub and flew. He soared on the wings of the wind.
He hid himself in darkness, making a shelter around himself from dark waters and thick clouds.
From the brightness before him came thick clouds, hailstones, and burning coals.
The LORD thundered in the sky. The Most High raised his voice with hailstones and burning coals.
He shot his arrows and scattered his enemies. He sent lightning bolts and drove them away.
The channels of the waters came into view. The world’s foundations lay bare when you rebuked them, LORD, at the blast of breath from your nostrils.
He reached down from above, took hold of me, and pulled me out of deep waters.
He rescued me from my powerful enemy and from those who hated me, because they were stronger than I was.
They came for me when disaster struck, but the LORD held me up.
He brought me into a wide-open place. He rescued me because he delighted in me.
The LORD rewarded me for doing what was right. He repaid me because my hands were clean.
I’ve followed the ways of the LORD and haven’t turned away from my God to do evil.
I kept all his judgments in front of me and never put his laws aside.
I lived blamelessly before him and kept myself from wrongdoing.
So the LORD has rewarded me for doing what is right, because he saw that my hands were clean.
You show mercy to those who show mercy and deal with integrity toward those who live with integrity.
You show yourself pure to the pure and outsmart those who are crooked.
You rescue people who are suffering, and you bring down those who look at others with pride.
You light my lamp, LORD. My God lights up my darkness.
With you I can charge through a troop. With my God I can leap over a wall.
God’s way is perfect. The LORD’s word has stood the test. He shields all who take refuge in him.
Who is God besides the LORD? Who is a rock besides our God,
the God who gives me strength and makes my way blameless?
He gives me feet like a deer’s and sets me securely on the heights.
He trains my hands for battle, so my arms can bend a bronze bow.
You’ve given me the shield of your salvation. Your right hand holds me up, and your gentleness has made me great.
You’ve made room for me to take wide steps, and my feet haven’t slipped.
I’ll chase my enemies and catch them. I won’t turn back until they’re finished.
I’ll strike them so they can’t get back up. They’ll fall beneath my feet.
You gave me strength for battle and brought down everyone who rose against me.
You made my enemies turn and run so I could cut down those who hated me.
They cried out, but no one saved them. They even called to the LORD, but he didn’t answer.
I crushed them like dust in the wind and threw them out like mud from the streets.
You rescued me from the people’s quarrels and made me head over nations. People I’ve never known will serve me.
As soon as they hear of me, they’ll obey. People from other lands will submit to me.
They’ll lose heart and come trembling out of their strongholds.
The LORD lives! Bless my rock! Let the God who saves me be lifted high,
the God who avenges me and brings peoples under my rule.
He rescues me from my enemies. You raise me above those who rise against me and save me from violent people.
So I’ll thank you among the nations, LORD, and sing praises to your name.
He gives his king great victories and shows faithful love to his anointed, to David and his descendants forever.
For the music director. A psalm by David. The heavens tell of God’s glory. The sky shows what his hands have made.
Day after day they pour out words, and night after night they reveal what they know.
There’s no speech or language where their voice goes unheard.
Their voice reaches across the earth, their words to the ends of the world. God has pitched a tent in the heavens for the sun,
which comes out like a groom leaving his room, like a strong runner eager to run the course.
It rises at one end of the heavens and makes its way to the other. Nothing escapes its heat.
The LORD’s instruction is perfect and restores the soul. His covenant is sure and gives wisdom to the inexperienced.
The LORD’s instructions are right and fill the heart with joy. His command is pure and gives light to the eyes.
The fear of the LORD is clean and lasts forever. His judgments are true and completely right.
They’re worth wanting more than gold, even piles of pure gold. They’re sweeter than honey straight from the comb.
They warn me, your servant. There’s great reward in keeping them.
Who can see all their own mistakes? Forgive the wrongs I don’t see.
Keep me, your servant, from sins I commit in defiance. Don’t let them rule over me. Then I’ll live uprightly, cleared of serious wrongdoing.
May the words I speak and the thoughts in my heart please you, LORD, my rock and my redeemer.
For the music director. A psalm by David. May the LORD answer you when trouble comes. May the name of the God of Jacob lift you out of danger.
May he send you help from the sanctuary and support you from Zion.
May he remember every offering you’ve brought and accept your burnt sacrifice. Selah.
May he give you what your heart desires and bring all your plans to pass.
We’ll shout for joy when you’re saved and raise our banners in the name of our God. May the LORD grant all you ask.
Now I know the LORD saves his anointed. He’ll answer from his holy heaven with the saving power of his right hand.
Some trust in chariots and others in horses, but we trust in the name of the LORD our God.
They buckle and fall, but we rise and stand firm.
Save us, LORD! May the King answer us when we call!
For the music director. A psalm by David. The king rejoices in your strength, LORD! He’s full of joy because you saved him.
You gave him what his heart wanted and granted what he asked for. Selah.
You came to meet him with good blessings and set a crown of pure gold on his head.
He asked you for life, and you gave it to him, a life that goes on forever and ever.
The victory you gave him brought him great glory. You clothed him in honor and majesty.
You bless him forever and fill him with joy in your presence.
The king trusts in the LORD. Because of the faithful love of the Most High, he won’t be shaken.
Your hand will find all your enemies. Your right hand will catch those who hate you.
When your anger rises, you’ll make them like a blazing furnace. The LORD will swallow them up in his wrath, and fire will consume them.
You’ll wipe out their descendants from the earth and their offspring from among humanity.
They meant to harm you and plotted evil against you, but their plans won’t succeed.
You’ll make them turn and run when you aim your drawn bows at them.
Rise high in your strength, LORD! We’ll sing and praise your power.
For the music director, to the tune of “The Doe of the Morning.” A psalm by David. My God, my God, why have you abandoned me? Why are you so far away when I groan for help?
My God, I cry out by day and you don’t answer. At night I keep crying.
Yet you are holy, enthroned in the praises of Israel.
Our ancestors trusted you. They trusted, and you rescued them.
They cried out to you and escaped. They trusted you and weren’t let down.
But I’m a worm, hardly human in their eyes. People scorn and despise me.
Everyone who sees me mocks me. They sneer and shake their heads, saying,
“He trusts the LORD. Let the LORD save him. Let him rescue him if he delights in him so much.”
Yet you brought me out of the womb. You taught me to trust you at my mother’s breast.
From birth I was placed in your care. You’ve been my God since my mother bore me.
Stay close to me, because trouble is near and there’s no one to help.
Many bulls have surrounded me. Mighty bulls from Bashan have closed in on me.
They open their mouths wide at me like lions roaring and tearing their prey.
I’m poured out like water. All my bones are out of joint. My heart is like wax melting inside me.
My strength has dried up like a shard of pottery, and my tongue sticks to the roof of my mouth. You’ve brought me down into the dust of death.
Dogs have surrounded me. A gang of evildoers has closed in on me. They’ve pierced my hands and feet.
I can count all my bones. They stare at me.
They divide my clothes among themselves and cast lots for what I’m wearing.
But LORD, stay close. You’re my help. Hurry to help me!
Save me from the sword. Save my precious life from the power of the dog.
Save me from the lion’s mouth! You’ve rescued me from the horns of wild oxen.
I’ll tell my brothers about your name. I’ll praise you in the middle of the assembly.
Praise the LORD, all you who fear him! Give him glory, all you descendants of Jacob! Stand in awe of him, all you descendants of Israel!
He took the suffering of the afflicted seriously and never turned his face away. When they cried to him, he listened.
You give me reason to praise you in the great assembly. I’ll keep my vows before those who fear you.
The humble will eat until they’re satisfied. Those who seek the LORD will praise him. May your hearts live forever!
People across the earth will remember and turn to the LORD. Every family of the nations will worship before you.
The kingdom belongs to the LORD. He rules over the nations.
All the wealthy on earth will eat and worship. All who go down to the dust will bow before him, even those who cannot keep themselves alive.
Their descendants will serve him. Generations to come will hear about the Lord.
They’ll come and tell people yet to be born about his righteousness, because he has done it.
A psalm by David. The LORD is my shepherd. I have everything I need.
He lets me rest in green pastures and leads me beside quiet waters.
He restores my soul. He guides me along paths of righteousness for the sake of his name.
Even when I walk through the valley where death casts its shadow, I won’t fear any evil, because you’re with me. Your rod and your staff comfort me.
You set a table for me in front of my enemies. You pour oil on my head, and my cup overflows.
Your goodness and faithful love will follow me every day of my life, and I’ll live in the LORD’s house forever.
A psalm by David. The earth and everything in it belong to the LORD, the world and everyone who lives in it.
He laid its foundations on the seas and set it firmly over the waters.
Who can climb the LORD’s hill? Who can stand in his holy place?
Those with clean hands and pure hearts, who don’t give themselves to what is false or swear an oath to deceive.
They’ll receive a blessing from the LORD and righteousness from the God who saves them.
This is the generation that seeks him, the people of Jacob who seek your face. Selah.
Lift up your heads, gates! Rise up, ancient doors, so the King of glory can come in.
Who is the King of glory? The LORD, strong and mighty. The LORD, mighty in battle.
Lift up your heads, gates! Lift them up, ancient doors, so the King of glory can come in.
Who is this King of glory? The LORD of Armies is the King of glory! Selah.
By David. LORD, I lift up my soul to you.
My God, I trust you. Keep me from shame. Don’t let my enemies win over me.
No one who waits for you will be put to shame. Shame will fall on those who betray others without cause.
Show me your ways, LORD. Teach me your paths.
Lead me in your truth and teach me, because you’re the God who saves me. I wait for you all day long.
Remember your tender mercy and faithful love, LORD. They’ve been there from long ago.
Forget the sins and wrongs of my youth. Remember me with faithful love because you are good, LORD.
The LORD is good and upright, so he teaches sinners the way to go.
He leads the humble in what is just and teaches them his way.
Every path the LORD takes shows faithful love and truth to those who keep his covenant and follow his teachings.
For the sake of your name, LORD, forgive my guilt, because it’s great.
Who are those who fear the LORD? He’ll teach them which path to choose.
They’ll live at ease, and their descendants will inherit the land.
The LORD is a friend to those who fear him. He makes his covenant known to them.
My eyes are always on the LORD, because he’ll pull my feet out of the net.
Turn toward me and have mercy on me, because I’m alone and suffering.
The troubles in my heart keep growing. Bring me out of my distress.
See my suffering and pain, and forgive all my sins.
Look at how many enemies I have. They hate me with a cruel hatred.
Guard my life and rescue me. Keep me from being let down, because I take refuge in you.
Let integrity and uprightness protect me, because I wait for you.
God, rescue Israel from all its troubles.
By David. Judge me, LORD, because I’ve lived with integrity and trusted you without wavering.
Examine me, LORD, and put me to the test. Search my heart and mind.
I keep your faithful love before my eyes and live by your truth.
I’ve never sat with liars, and I won’t join people who pretend to be what they aren’t.
I hate the gatherings of evildoers and won’t sit with the wicked.
I’ll wash my hands in innocence and walk around your altar, LORD,
so I can thank you aloud and tell of all your wonderful deeds.
LORD, I love the house where you live, the place where your glory dwells.
Don’t take my life along with sinners or sweep me away with bloodthirsty people.
Their hands are busy with evil, and their right hands are full of bribes.
But I’ll keep living with integrity. Redeem me and have mercy on me.
My feet stand on level ground. I’ll bless the LORD in the gatherings of his people.
By David. The LORD is my light and my salvation. Who should I fear? The LORD is the stronghold of my life. Who could frighten me?
When evildoers came to devour me, my enemies and attackers were the ones who stumbled and fell.
Even if an army camps against me, my heart won’t fear. Even if war breaks out against me, I’ll still stand confident.
I’ve asked the LORD for one thing, and I’ll keep seeking it: to live in his house all my days, to see his beauty and seek him in his temple.
When trouble comes, he’ll keep me safe in his shelter. He’ll hide me deep inside his tent and set me high on a rock.
Then my head will rise above the enemies around me. I’ll offer sacrifices with shouts of joy in his tent and sing praises to the LORD.
Hear me when I cry out, LORD. Have mercy on me and answer me.
When you said, “Seek my face,” my heart answered, “LORD, I’ll seek your face.”
Don’t hide your face from me or send your servant away in anger. You’ve been my help. Don’t leave me or abandon me, God who saves me.
Even if my father and mother leave me, the LORD will take me in.
Teach me your way, LORD. Lead me on a straight path with my enemies around me.
Don’t hand me over to what my enemies want. False witnesses have risen against me, breathing threats.
I still believe I’ll see the LORD’s goodness in the land of the living.
Wait for the LORD. Be strong and take heart. Yes, wait for the LORD.
By David. LORD, I call to you. My rock, don’t shut your ears to me. If you stay silent, I’ll be like those who go down to the pit.
Hear my plea when I cry to you and lift my hands toward your Most Holy Place.
Don’t drag me away with the wicked, with people who speak peace to their neighbors while they plan harm in their hearts.
Pay them back for what they’ve done and for the evil in their actions. Give them what their own hands have earned.
They pay no attention to what the LORD does or to what his hands have made. He’ll tear them down and never build them up again.
Blessed be the LORD, because he heard my plea for help.
The LORD is my strength and my shield. I trusted him with my heart, and he helped me. My heart is full of joy, and I’ll thank him with my song.
The LORD is his people’s strength. He’s a stronghold that saves his anointed.
Save your people and bless those who are your inheritance. Shepherd them and carry them forever.
A psalm by David. Give the LORD glory and strength, you sons of the mighty.
Give the LORD the glory his name deserves. Worship him in holy splendor.
The LORD’s voice rolls over the waters. The God of glory thunders, the LORD over the vast waters.
The LORD’s voice is powerful. His voice is full of majesty.
The LORD’s voice breaks the cedars. The LORD shatters the cedars of Lebanon.
He makes Lebanon skip like a calf and Sirion like a young wild ox.
The LORD’s voice strikes with flashes of lightning.
The LORD’s voice shakes the wilderness. The LORD shakes the wilderness of Kadesh.
The LORD’s voice makes the deer give birth and strips the forests bare. In his temple everything cries, “Glory!”
The LORD sat on his throne at the Flood. The LORD reigns as King forever.
The LORD gives his people strength. The LORD blesses his people with peace.
A psalm by David. A song for the dedication of the temple. I’ll praise you, LORD, because you lifted me up and gave my enemies no chance to gloat over me.
LORD my God, I cried out to you, and you healed me.
LORD, you pulled me up from Sheol. You kept me alive when I was close to going down to the pit.
Sing praise to the LORD, you who are faithful to him. Give thanks to his holy name.
His anger lasts a moment, and his favor lasts a lifetime. Weeping may stay the night, but joy comes in the morning.
When life was going well for me, I said, “Nothing will ever shake me.”
LORD, when you favored me, you made my mountain stand firm. When you hid your face, I was shaken.
I cried out to you, LORD. I pleaded with you:
“What good would come from my death if I went down to the pit? Will dust praise you or tell of your faithfulness?
Hear me, LORD, and have mercy on me. LORD, come help me.”
You turned my mourning into dancing. You took off my clothes of grief and dressed me in joy,
so my heart could sing praises to you and never go quiet. LORD my God, I’ll thank you forever!
For the music director. A psalm by David. LORD, I take refuge in you. Never let me be put to shame. Rescue me in your righteousness.
Lean down and listen to me. Rescue me quickly. Be my solid rock, a fortress where I can be safe.
You are my rock and my fortress. For the sake of your name, lead me and guide me.
Pull me out of the net they’ve hidden for me, because you’re my stronghold.
I place my spirit in your hands. You redeem me, LORD, God of truth.
I hate those who cling to worthless idols, but I trust in the LORD.
I’ll rejoice in your faithful love, because you’ve seen my suffering and known me through my troubles.
You haven’t handed me over to the enemy. You’ve set my feet in a wide-open place.
Have mercy on me, LORD, because I’m in distress. My eyes, my soul, and my body are wearing away with grief.
My life drains away in sorrow and my years in sighing. My guilt saps my strength, and my bones waste away.
Because of my enemies, my neighbors look down on me and people I know are horrified by me. When they see me on the street, they run away.
They’ve forgotten me as if I were dead. I’m like a broken pot.
I hear people slandering me. Terror is all around. They conspire together and plot to take my life.
But I trust you, LORD. I say, “You’re my God.”
My times are in your hands. Rescue me from my enemies and from those who pursue me.
Let your face shine on your servant. Save me in your faithful love.
LORD, I’ve called on you. Keep me from shame. Let the wicked be put to shame and go silent in Sheol.
Silence those lying lips that speak against the righteous with pride and contempt.
How great is the goodness you’ve stored up for those who fear you, the goodness you show in front of everyone to those who take refuge in you!
You hide them in the shelter of your presence from people’s schemes. You keep them safe in your dwelling, away from quarrels and accusations.
Praise the LORD! He showed me his wonderful faithful love in a fortified city.
I panicked and said, “I’ve been cut off from your sight.” Yet when I cried to you for help, you heard my plea.
Love the LORD, all you who are faithful to him! The LORD protects the faithful and pays the arrogant back in full.
Be strong and take heart, all you who put your hope in the LORD.
By David. A psalm for reflection. Blessed is the person whose rebellion is forgiven and whose sin is covered.
Blessed is the one whose guilt the LORD doesn’t count against them and whose spirit holds no deceit.
When I kept quiet, my bones wasted away as I groaned all day long.
Day and night your hand weighed on me. My strength dried up in the summer heat. Selah.
I admitted my sin to you and stopped hiding my guilt. I said, “I’ll confess my wrongs to the LORD,” and you forgave the guilt of my sin. Selah.
So let all who are faithful pray to you while you can be found. When the floodwaters rise, they won’t reach them.
You’re my hiding place. You’ll keep me safe from trouble and surround me with songs of rescue. Selah.
I’ll teach you which way to go. I’ll guide you and keep my eye on you.
Don’t be like a horse or mule that has no understanding and needs a bit and bridle to make it come near.
The wicked face many sorrows, but faithful love surrounds those who trust in the LORD.
Be glad in the LORD and rejoice, you righteous people! Shout for joy, all whose hearts are upright!
Rejoice in the LORD, you righteous people! Praise belongs on the lips of those who live uprightly.
Thank the LORD with the lyre. Sing praise to him with a ten-stringed harp.
Sing him a new song. Play it well and shout for joy!
The LORD’s word is right, and he’s faithful in everything he does.
He loves righteousness and justice. The earth is full of the LORD’s faithful love.
The heavens came into being by the LORD’s word, and all their hosts by the breath of his mouth.
He gathers the sea into a heap and stores the deep waters away.
Let the whole earth fear the LORD. Let everyone who lives in the world stand in awe of him.
He spoke and it came to be. He gave the command and it stood firm.
The LORD brings the nations’ plans to nothing and stops the peoples’ schemes from succeeding.
The LORD’s plans stand firm forever. What he intends lasts through every generation.
Blessed is the nation whose God is the LORD, the people he chose as his inheritance.
The LORD looks down from heaven and sees all humanity.
From where he lives, he watches everyone on earth.
He’s the one who formed all their hearts, and he takes notice of everything they do.
A huge army can’t save a king, and great strength can’t rescue a warrior.
A horse is a false hope for safety. All its power can’t save anyone.
The LORD watches over those who fear him and put their hope in his faithful love,
to rescue them from death and keep them alive through famine.
We wait for the LORD with our whole being. He’s our help and our shield.
Our hearts rejoice in him because we trust in his holy name.
Let your faithful love rest on us, LORD, as we put our hope in you.
By David, when he pretended to be insane before Abimelech, who drove him away. I’ll bless the LORD at all times. His praise will always be on my lips.
With my whole soul I’ll boast in the LORD. Let the humble hear it and be glad.
Praise the greatness of the LORD with me. Let’s lift up his name together.
I sought the LORD, and he answered me. He rescued me from all my fears.
Those who look to him shine with joy. Shame will never cover their faces.
I was poor and cried out, and the LORD heard me. He saved me from all my troubles.
The angel of the LORD camps around those who fear him and rescues them.
Taste and see that the LORD is good. Blessed are those who take refuge in him.
Fear the LORD, you who belong to him. Those who fear him have all they need.
Even young lions go hungry, but those who seek the LORD won’t lack any good thing.
Come, children, listen to me. I’ll teach you what it means to fear the LORD.
Who wants to live a long life and enjoy good days?
Keep your tongue from evil and your lips from lies.
Turn away from evil and do good. Seek peace and go after it.
The LORD watches over those who do right and listens when they cry out.
The LORD sets his face against those who do evil, to wipe the memory of them from the earth.
The righteous cry out, and the LORD hears them. He rescues them from all their troubles.
The LORD stays close to the brokenhearted and saves those whose spirits are crushed.
The righteous face many troubles, but the LORD rescues them from every one.
He guards all their bones. Every one stays whole.
Evil will kill the wicked. Those who hate the righteous will be condemned.
The LORD redeems the lives of his servants. Everyone who takes refuge in him will escape condemnation.
By David. LORD, take up my cause against those who accuse me. Fight against those who fight me.
Take up your shields, large and small, and stand up to help me.
Raise your spear and block those chasing me. Tell my soul, “I am the one who saves you.”
Let those who want me dead be put to shame and dishonor. Turn back and confuse those who plot my ruin.
Let them scatter like chaff in the wind, with the LORD’s angel driving them away.
Let their path be dark and slippery, with the LORD’s angel chasing them.
For no reason they hid a net for me in a pit. For no reason they dug a pit to take my life.
Let ruin overtake them by surprise. Let them get caught in the net they hid and fall into their own ruin.
Then my soul will rejoice in the LORD and celebrate his rescue.
Every bone in my body will say, “LORD, who is like you? You rescue the poor from people too strong for them and save the poor and needy from those who rob them.”
False witnesses stand up against me and question me about things I know nothing about.
They repay my good with evil, leaving me heartbroken.
When they were sick, I wore sackcloth and humbled myself by fasting. My prayer came back to my own heart.
I treated them as I would a friend or a brother. I bowed my head in grief as if I were mourning my mother.
But when I was in trouble they celebrated and gathered against me. Attackers came together without my knowing, and they tore at me without stopping.
Like godless people mocking at a feast, they gnashed their teeth at me.
Lord, how long will you stand by and watch? Rescue me from their attacks. Save my precious life from the lions.
I’ll thank you in the great assembly and praise you among crowds of people.
Don’t let those who are my enemies without cause celebrate my downfall. Don’t let those who hate me for no reason wink at each other.
They speak no words of peace. They make up lies against people who live quietly in the land.
They open their mouths wide against me and say, “Aha! Aha! We saw it ourselves!”
But you saw it, LORD. Don’t stay silent. Lord, don’t stay far from me.
Wake up and rise to defend me, my God! My Lord, take up my case!
Clear my name, LORD my God, according to your righteousness. Don’t let them gloat over me.
Don’t let them think, “Aha! This is exactly what we wanted!” Don’t let them say, “We swallowed him up!”
Let those who celebrate my trouble be put to shame and confusion together. Dress those who boast over me in shame and dishonor.
Let those who stand with me in my just cause shout for joy. Let them keep saying, “Great is the LORD, who delights in his servant’s well-being!”
I’ll speak of your righteousness and sing your praise all day long.
For the music director. By David, the LORD’s servant. This is what I’ve come to understand about the rebellion of the wicked: they live with no fear of God.
They think too highly of themselves to see their own sin and hate it.
Their words are full of evil and deceit. They’ve stopped acting wisely or doing good.
They lie in bed plotting wrong. They set out on a path that leads to no good and refuse to reject evil.
LORD, your faithful love reaches to the heavens, and your faithfulness reaches to the skies.
Your righteousness is like the mountains of God. Your judgments are like the depths of the sea. LORD, you keep people and animals alive.
How precious is your faithful love, God! People take refuge in the shadow of your wings.
They feast on the abundance of your house. You let them drink from your river of delights.
The spring of life is with you. In your light we see light.
Keep showing faithful love to those who know you and righteousness to those whose hearts are upright.
Don’t let the proud trample me or the wicked drive me away.
Look, those who do evil have fallen. They’re knocked down and can’t rise.
By David. Don’t wear yourself out worrying about people who do evil, and don’t envy those who do wrong.
Soon they’ll be cut down like grass and wither like green plants.
Trust the LORD and do good. Live in the land and find safety there.
Take delight in the LORD, and he’ll give you what your heart desires.
Put your life in the LORD’s hands. Trust him, and he’ll act:
he’ll make your righteousness shine like the light and your justice like the sun at noon.
Be still before the LORD and wait patiently for him. Don’t worry when people prosper by carrying out wicked plans.
Let go of anger and turn away from rage. Worrying over them only leads to doing wrong.
Evildoers will be cut off, and those who wait for the LORD will inherit the land.
Before long the wicked will be gone. You’ll look where they lived, and they won’t be there.
The humble will inherit the land and enjoy peace in abundance.
The wicked plot against the righteous and grind their teeth at them.
The Lord laughs at them because he sees their day is coming.
The wicked draw their swords and bend their bows to bring down the poor and needy and kill people who walk uprightly.
Their swords will pierce their own hearts, and their bows will be broken.
The little a righteous person has is better than the wealth of many wicked people.
The strength of the wicked will be broken, and the LORD will hold up the righteous.
The LORD knows the days of those who live with integrity. Their inheritance will last forever.
They won’t be put to shame in hard times. Even in famine they’ll have enough.
The wicked will perish. The LORD’s enemies will fade like the beauty of the fields. They’ll disappear like smoke.
The wicked borrow and never pay back. The righteous give freely.
Those the LORD blesses will inherit the land. Those he curses will be cut off.
The LORD makes a person’s steps firm and delights in the path they take.
Even if they stumble, they won’t fall, because the LORD holds them by the hand.
I was young once and now I’m old, and I’ve never seen the righteous abandoned or their children begging for bread.
They’re generous all day long and lend to others. Their children are blessed.
Turn away from evil and do good, and you’ll live securely forever.
The LORD loves justice and never leaves those who are faithful to him. He keeps them safe forever, but the children of the wicked will be cut off.
The righteous will inherit the land and live there forever.
The righteous speak with wisdom and say what is just.
They carry God’s instruction in their hearts, so their feet won’t slip.
The wicked lie in wait for the righteous and look for a chance to kill them.
The LORD won’t leave them in the hands of the wicked or let them be condemned at trial.
Wait for the LORD and stay on his path. He’ll lift you up to inherit the land. You’ll see it when the wicked are cut off.
I’ve seen a wicked person with great power, spreading out like a green tree in its own soil.
Then they passed away and were gone. I looked for them, but they were nowhere to be found.
Pay attention to people who live with integrity. Watch those who do right, because there’s a future for people who make peace.
People who rebel will be destroyed together. The future of the wicked will be cut off.
The LORD saves the righteous. He’s their stronghold in times of trouble.
The LORD helps and rescues them. He saves them from the wicked because they’ve taken refuge in him.
A psalm by David, for remembrance. LORD, don’t rebuke me in your wrath or discipline me in your burning anger.
Your arrows have pierced me, and your hand weighs heavily on me.
My whole body is sick because of your anger. My bones have no peace because of my sin.
My wrongs have risen over my head. They’re a burden too heavy for me to carry.
My wounds fester and stink because of my foolishness.
I’m in pain and bent low. I spend the whole day mourning.
My sides burn with pain. My whole body is sick.
I’m weak and badly bruised. I groan because my heart is in anguish.
Lord, you know everything I long for. You hear all my groaning.
My heart pounds. My strength is gone, and the light has left my eyes.
My loved ones and friends keep away from my suffering. Even my family stands far off.
Those who want me dead lay traps for me. Those who want to hurt me make threats and plot lies all day long.
But I act as though I can’t hear, as though I can’t speak.
I’m like someone who hears nothing and has no reply to give.
I put my hope in you, LORD. You’ll answer me, Lord my God.
I said, “Don’t let them gloat over me or boast when I lose my footing.”
I’m about to fall, and my pain never leaves me.
I’ll confess what I’ve done wrong. I’m sorry for my sin.
My enemies are strong and many. So many people hate me for no reason.
They repay good with evil and oppose me because I pursue what is good.
Don’t leave me, LORD. My God, stay close to me.
Hurry to help me, Lord, my salvation.
For the music director. For Jeduthun. A psalm by David. I said, “I’ll watch how I act so I don’t sin with my tongue. I’ll keep a tight rein on my mouth while the wicked are in front of me.”
I stayed completely silent and held back even good words. My sorrow only grew.
My heart burned inside me. The more I thought about it, the hotter the fire burned. Then I spoke:
“LORD, show me where my life ends and how many days I have. Let me see how fleeting I am.
You’ve made my days only a few handbreadths long. My whole life is nothing before you. Every person is only a breath.” Selah.
“People go about like shadows, busying themselves for nothing. They pile up wealth without knowing who will collect it.
And now, Lord, what am I waiting for? My hope is in you.
Save me from all my rebellion. Don’t let fools make me an object of scorn.
I stayed silent and didn’t open my mouth, because you were the one who did it.
Take this punishment away from me. The blow of your hand has worn me out.
When you correct someone for doing wrong, you eat away at what they treasure like a moth. Every person is only a breath.” Selah.
“Hear my prayer, LORD, and listen to my cry. Don’t stay silent when you see my tears. I’m a stranger staying with you, a traveler like all my ancestors.
Spare me so I can regain my strength before I go away and am gone for good.”
For the music director. A psalm by David. I waited patiently for the LORD. He turned toward me and heard my cry.
He pulled me out of a dreadful pit, out of the sticky mud. He set my feet on a rock and gave me firm footing.
He put a new song in my mouth, a song of praise to our God. Many will see what he’s done, stand in awe, and trust the LORD.
Blessed are those who put their trust in the LORD and turn away from the proud and from people who chase lies.
LORD my God, you’ve done so many wonders and made so many plans for us. If I tried to tell you about them all, they’d be more than I could count.
You didn’t want sacrifice or offering. You opened my ears. You didn’t require a burnt offering or a sin offering.
Then I said, “Here I am. What is written about me is in the scroll.
I take joy in doing your will, my God. Your instruction is in my heart.”
I’ve announced the good news of your righteousness in the great assembly. You know, LORD, that I won’t keep quiet.
I haven’t kept your righteousness to myself. I’ve told of your faithfulness and your salvation. I haven’t hidden your faithful love or your truth from the great assembly.
LORD, don’t hold back your tender mercy from me. Keep me safe always with your faithful love and truth.
Troubles beyond counting surround me. My wrongs have caught up with me, and I can’t lift my eyes. They outnumber the hairs on my head, and my courage is gone.
Please rescue me, LORD. Hurry to help me, LORD.
Let those who want to take my life be put to shame and confusion together. Turn back and disgrace those who enjoy seeing me hurt.
Let their own shame leave them devastated when they say to me, “Aha! Aha!”
Let all who seek you rejoice and be glad in you. Let those who love your salvation keep saying, “How great is the LORD!”
I’m poor and needy. Lord, remember me. You’re my help and my rescuer. My God, don’t delay.
For the music director. A psalm by David. Blessed are those who look after the poor. The LORD will rescue them when trouble comes.
The LORD will protect them and keep them alive. They’ll be blessed in the land, and he won’t hand them over to their enemies.
The LORD will sustain them on their sickbed and help them get well again.
I said, “LORD, have mercy on me. Heal me, because I’ve sinned against you.”
My enemies say cruel things about me: “When will he die and his name be forgotten?”
When one of them visits, he tells me lies. He looks for something harmful to say about me and spreads it as soon as he leaves.
Everyone who hates me whispers about me together. They imagine the worst for me.
“A terrible illness has struck him,” they say. “He’s down, and he’ll never get back up.”
Even my close friend, the one I trusted and shared my bread with, has turned against me.
But you, LORD, have mercy on me. Raise me up so I can repay them.
I know you delight in me because my enemy hasn’t triumphed over me.
You uphold me in my integrity and give me a place in your presence forever.
Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting! Amen and amen.
For the music director. A psalm for reflection by the sons of Korah. Like a deer panting for streams of water, my soul longs for you, God.
My soul thirsts for God, the living God. When can I come and stand before him?
My tears have been my food day and night, while people keep asking, “Where is your God?”
I pour out my soul as I remember how I walked with the crowd and led them to God’s house, a festival crowd shouting for joy and singing praise.
Why are you so downcast, my soul? Why are you so restless inside me? Put your hope in God. I’ll praise him again for the rescue his presence brings.
My God, my soul is downcast within me. So I remember you from the land of the Jordan, from the heights of Hermon, and from Mount Mizar.
Deep calls to deep in the roar of your waterfalls. All your waves and surges have swept over me.
By day the LORD sends his faithful love. At night his song stays with me, a prayer to the God of my life.
I say to God, my rock, “Why have you forgotten me? Why do I go around grieving under my enemy’s oppression?”
My enemies’ taunts cut like a sword in my bones. They keep asking me, “Where is your God?”
Why are you so downcast, my soul? Why are you so restless inside me? Put your hope in God. I’ll praise him again, my Savior and my God.
Clear my name, God. Take up my case against a godless nation. Rescue me from people who lie and do evil.
You’re the God who gives me strength. Why have you rejected me? Why do I walk around grieving under my enemy’s oppression?
Send out your light and your truth. Let them guide me and bring me to your holy hill, to the place where you live.
Then I’ll go to God’s altar, to God, my greatest joy. I’ll praise you with the harp, God, my God.
Why are you so downcast, my soul? Why are you so restless inside me? Put your hope in God. I’ll praise him again, my Savior, my helper, and my God.
For the music director. A psalm for reflection by the sons of Korah. God, we’ve heard it with our own ears. Our ancestors told us what you did in their time, long ago.
With your own hand you drove out nations and planted our ancestors in their place. You struck those peoples and gave our ancestors room to spread.
They didn’t win the land by their swords or save themselves by their strength. Your right hand, your strong arm, and the light of your face won it for them, because you favored them.
You are my King, God. Give the command that brings Jacob victory!
Through you we’ll push back our enemies. In your name we’ll trample those who rise against us.
I won’t put my trust in my bow, and my sword can’t save me.
You saved us from our enemies and put those who hate us to shame.
All day long we’ve boasted in God. We’ll thank your name forever. Selah.
But now you’ve rejected us and brought us to shame. You no longer go out with our armies.
You make us turn and run from the enemy. Those who hate us take whatever they want.
You’ve handed us over like sheep for food and scattered us among the nations.
You sold your people for nothing. You gained nothing from the sale.
You’ve made us a disgrace to our neighbors. Everyone around us mocks and ridicules us.
You’ve made us a joke among the nations. People shake their heads at us.
My disgrace is in front of me all day long, and shame covers my face,
because of the insults of those who mock and abuse me, because of the enemy who wants revenge.
All this has happened to us, yet we haven’t forgotten you or broken faith with your covenant.
Our hearts haven’t turned away, and our feet haven’t strayed from your path,
even though you’ve crushed us in a place where jackals live and covered us with the shadow of death.
If we had forgotten our God’s name or stretched out our hands to another god,
wouldn’t God find out? He knows the secrets of the heart.
For your sake we face death all day long. People treat us like sheep ready for slaughter.
Wake up, Lord! Why are you sleeping? Rise up! Don’t reject us forever.
Why do you hide your face and forget our suffering and oppression?
We’ve sunk down into the dust. Our bodies cling to the ground.
Rise up to help us. Rescue us because of your faithful love.

For the music director, to the tune of “The Lilies.” A psalm for reflection by the sons of Korah. A wedding song. My heart overflows with a noble theme. I recite my verses for the king. My tongue is like the pen of a skilled writer.
You surpass all other men. Grace pours from your lips, because God has blessed you forever.
Strap your sword to your thigh, mighty one. Put on your splendor and majesty.
Ride out in majesty to victory for truth, humility, and righteousness. Let your right hand do deeds that fill people with awe.
Your arrows are sharp. Nations fall beneath you as your arrows pierce the hearts of the king’s enemies.
Your throne, God, lasts forever and ever. The scepter of your kingdom is a scepter of justice.
You love righteousness and hate wickedness. That’s why God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of joy above your companions.
All your clothes are fragrant with myrrh, aloes, and cassia. Music from stringed instruments in ivory palaces makes you glad.
Daughters of kings are among the women you honor. At your right hand stands the queen in gold from Ophir.
Listen, daughter. Pay close attention. Leave your people and your father’s household behind.
The king will desire your beauty. Honor him, because he is your lord.
The daughter of Tyre will bring a gift. The richest people will seek your favor.
Inside, the princess is radiant. Gold is woven into her clothes.
She’ll be led to the king wearing embroidered robes. Her young companions will follow and be brought to you.
They’ll be led in with gladness and joy as they enter the king’s palace.
Your sons will take the place of your ancestors. You’ll make them princes throughout the land.
I’ll keep the memory of your name alive in every generation. The peoples will thank you forever and ever.
For the music director. By the sons of Korah. According to Alamoth. God is our refuge and strength, right here to help us in trouble.
So we won’t be afraid, even if the earth gives way and the mountains fall into the heart of the sea,
even if its waters roar and churn and the mountains shake as the waters surge. Selah.
There’s a river whose streams bring joy to the city of God, the holy place where the Most High lives.
God is in the city, so it won’t be shaken. At dawn God will come to its aid.
Nations raged and kingdoms shook. God raised his voice, and the earth melted.
The LORD of Armies is with us. The God of Jacob is our refuge. Selah.
Come and see what the LORD has done, the devastation he’s brought upon the earth.
He ends wars to the farthest corners of the earth. He breaks the bow, shatters the spear, and burns the chariots.
“Be still and know that I am God. I will be exalted among the nations. I will be exalted throughout the earth.”
The LORD of Armies is with us. The God of Jacob is our refuge. Selah.
For the music director. A psalm by the sons of Korah. Clap your hands, all you nations! Shout to God in triumph!
The LORD Most High fills us with awe. He’s the great King over all the earth.
He brings nations under our rule and puts peoples beneath our feet.
He chooses our inheritance for us, the pride of Jacob, whom he loved. Selah.
God has gone up to shouts of joy. The LORD has gone up to the sound of a trumpet.
Sing praises to God! Sing praises! Sing praises to our King! Sing praises!
God is King over all the earth. Sing praise with understanding.
God reigns over the nations. God sits on his holy throne.
The leaders of the peoples gather as the people of Abraham’s God. The shields of the earth belong to God. He is exalted far above all!
A song. A psalm by the sons of Korah. Great is the LORD and worthy of great praise in the city of our God, on his holy mountain.
Mount Zion rises beautifully in the far north, the joy of the whole earth, the city of the great King.
God has shown himself to be a refuge inside its fortresses.
Look, the kings gathered and advanced together.
When they saw the city, they were stunned. They panicked and hurried away.
Trembling seized them there, with pain like that of a woman in labor.
With an east wind you shatter the ships of Tarshish.
What we heard about, we’ve now seen for ourselves in the city of the LORD of Armies, the city of our God. God will keep it standing forever. Selah.
Inside your temple, God, we think about your faithful love.
Your praise reaches the ends of the earth, just as your name does, God. Your right hand is full of righteousness.
Let Mount Zion be glad! Let the towns of Judah rejoice because of your judgments.
Walk around Zion. Circle it and count its towers.
Look closely at its walls and take in its palaces, so you can tell the next generation about them.
This God is our God forever and ever. He’ll guide us to the end of our lives.
For the music director. A psalm by the sons of Korah. Hear this, all you peoples. Listen, everyone who lives in the world,
people of high and low standing, rich and poor alike.
I’ll speak words of wisdom. What I’ve thought through in my heart will give understanding.
I’ll listen closely to a proverb and explain my riddle to the sound of the harp.
Why should I be afraid when trouble comes and the evil of those at my heels closes in around me?
Some people trust in their wealth and boast about how much they own,
yet none of them can buy back the life of another or pay God a ransom for them.
The price of a life is too high. No payment is ever enough
to let someone live forever and never see decay.
Everyone can see that wise people die. Fools and the senseless die too, leaving their wealth to others.
They imagine their houses will stand forever, with descendants living there generation after generation. They name their lands after themselves.
But even with all their wealth, people don’t last. They die just like animals.
That’s the fate of those who live foolishly and of those who applaud what they say. Selah.
They’re like sheep marked for Sheol, with death as their shepherd. In the morning the upright will rule over them. Their beauty will decay in Sheol, far from their grand homes.
But God will rescue my life from the power of Sheol, because he’ll take me in. Selah.
Don’t be afraid when someone grows rich and their household grows more impressive.
When they die, they’ll take nothing with them. Their glory won’t follow them down.
They may congratulate themselves while they’re alive, and people may praise you when you do well for yourself,
but they’ll join their ancestors, who will never see the light again.
People who have wealth without understanding are like animals that perish.
A psalm by Asaph. The Mighty One, God, the LORD, speaks and summons the whole earth from sunrise to sunset.
God shines out from Zion, perfect in beauty.
Our God comes and won’t stay silent. Fire devours everything ahead of him, and a fierce storm rages around him.
He calls to the heavens above and to the earth as he comes to judge his people:
“Gather my faithful ones to me, those who made a covenant with me by sacrifice.”
The heavens declare his righteousness, because God himself is the judge. Selah.
“Listen, my people, and I’ll speak. Israel, I’ll testify against you. I am God, your God.
I have no complaint about your sacrifices. Your burnt offerings are always before me.
I don’t need a bull from your stall or male goats from your pens.
Every animal in the forest is mine, along with the cattle on a thousand hills.
I know every bird in the mountains, and all the wild animals of the fields are mine.
If I were hungry, I wouldn’t tell you. The world and everything in it belong to me.
Do I eat the flesh of bulls or drink the blood of goats?
Offer thanks to God as your sacrifice and keep the vows you made to the Most High.
Call on me when trouble comes. I’ll rescue you, and you’ll honor me.”
But God says to the wicked, “What right have you to recite my laws or speak my covenant,
when you hate correction and toss my words aside?
You see a thief and join in. You make common cause with adulterers.
You give your mouth over to evil, and your tongue spins lies.
You sit and speak against your brother. You slander your own mother’s son.
You did all this while I kept quiet, and you thought I was just like you. Now I’ll rebuke you and lay the charges out before your eyes.
Think about this, you who forget God, or I’ll tear you apart and no one will rescue you.
Those who offer thanks as a sacrifice honor me. To those who set their path right I’ll show the salvation of God.”

For the music director. A psalm by David, when Nathan the prophet came to him after he had slept with Bathsheba. Have mercy on me, God, because of your faithful love. In your great compassion, wipe away my rebellion.
Wash away all my guilt. Cleanse me from my sin.
I know what I’ve done wrong. My sin is always in front of me.
Against you, you alone, I’ve sinned and done what is evil in your sight. You are right when you speak and just when you judge.
I was born in guilt. Sin was there from the time my mother conceived me.
You want truth deep inside me. You teach me wisdom in the hidden places of my heart.
Cleanse me with hyssop, and I’ll be clean. Wash me, and I’ll be whiter than snow.
Let me hear joy and gladness again, so the bones you’ve broken can rejoice.
Turn your face away from my sins and wipe away all my guilt.
Create a clean heart in me, God, and renew a steadfast spirit within me.
Don’t send me away from your presence or take your Holy Spirit from me.
Give me back the joy of your salvation. Keep me going with a willing spirit.
Then I’ll teach those who rebel how to follow your ways, and sinners will turn back to you.
Free me from the guilt of bloodshed, God who saves me. Then I’ll sing aloud about your righteousness.
Lord, open my lips, and I’ll speak your praise.
You take no delight in sacrifice, or I’d bring one. A burnt offering brings you no pleasure.
The sacrifice God desires is a broken spirit. God, you welcome a broken heart that is sorry for its sin.
In your good pleasure, do good to Zion. Build up the walls of Jerusalem.
Then you’ll delight in sacrifices offered in righteousness, in burnt offerings and offerings burned whole. Then bulls will be offered on your altar.

For the music director. A psalm for reflection by David, when Doeg the Edomite went to Saul and said, “David has come to Ahimelech’s house.” Why do you boast about doing harm, mighty man? God’s faithful love lasts all day long.
Your tongue plots ruin, cutting like a sharp razor as you deceive.
You love evil more than good and would rather lie than tell the truth. Selah.
You love words that tear people apart, you lying tongue.
God will bring you down for good. He’ll grab you and pull you out of your tent. He’ll uproot you from the land of the living. Selah.
Those who do right will see it and stand in awe. They’ll laugh at him and say,
“Look at the man who refused to make God his strength. He trusted in his great wealth and drew his strength from doing wrong.”
But I’m like a green olive tree in God’s house. I trust in God’s faithful love forever and ever.
I’ll thank you forever for what you’ve done. In front of your faithful people I’ll put my hope in your name, because it is good.
For the music director, to the tune of “Mahalath.” A psalm for reflection by David. The fool says in their heart, “There is no God.” They’re corrupt and do terrible wrong. No one does good.
God looks down from heaven on humanity to see if anyone understands and seeks him.
Everyone has turned away. Together they’ve become corrupt. No one does good. No one at all.
Don’t these evildoers understand? They devour my people as casually as they eat bread, and they never call on God.
Terror seized them where there was nothing to fear. God scattered the bones of those who camped against you. You put them to shame because God rejected them.
If only Israel’s rescue would come from Zion! When God brings his people back from captivity, Jacob will rejoice and Israel will be glad.

For the music director, with stringed instruments. A psalm for reflection by David, when the Ziphites came to Saul and said, “Isn’t David hiding among us?” Save me by your name, God. Use your strength to clear my name.
Hear my prayer, God. Listen to the words I’m saying.
Strangers have risen up against me. Violent people are trying to take my life. They give no thought to God. Selah.
Look, God is my helper. The Lord is the one who keeps me alive.
He’ll pay my enemies back for their evil. In your faithfulness, bring them down.
I’ll bring you a sacrifice freely. I’ll thank you for your name, LORD, because it is good.
You’ve rescued me from every trouble, and I’ve seen my enemies defeated with my own eyes.
For the music director, with stringed instruments. A psalm for reflection by David. Listen to my prayer, God. Don’t hide from my plea.
Pay attention and answer me. I’m restless in my distress, and I groan
because of my enemy’s threats and the pressure of the wicked. They bring suffering on me and hold on to their anger against me.
My heart aches inside me. The terrors of death have fallen on me.
Fear and trembling have seized me. Horror has overwhelmed me.
I said, “If only I had wings like a dove! I’d fly away and find rest.
I’d go far away and stay out in the wilderness.” Selah.
“I’d hurry to find shelter from the howling wind and the storm.”
Lord, confuse them and scramble their words, because I’ve seen violence and conflict in the city.
Day and night they prowl along its walls. Malice and abuse fill the city.
Ruin is at work inside it. Threats and lies never leave its streets.
If an enemy had insulted me, I could have borne it. If someone who hated me had risen against me, I could have hidden from them.
But it was you, someone like me, my companion and close friend.
We enjoyed each other’s company and walked with the crowd into God’s house.
Let death catch them by surprise. Let them go down alive to Sheol, because wickedness lives in their homes and among them.
As for me, I’ll call on God, and the LORD will save me.
Evening, morning, and noon I cry out in distress, and he hears my voice.
He brought me safely out of the battle against me, even though many stood against me.
God, who has been on his throne forever, will hear and answer them. Selah. They refuse to change and have no fear of God.
My companion turned against his friends and broke his covenant.
His speech was smooth as butter, but his heart was set on war. His words were softer than oil, yet they were drawn swords.
Give your burden to the LORD, and he’ll sustain you. He’ll never let the righteous be shaken.
But you, God, will bring them down into the pit of destruction. Violent and deceitful people won’t live out half their days. I’ll put my trust in you.

For the music director, to the tune of “Silent Dove in Distant Lands.” A poem by David, when the Philistines seized him in Gath. Have mercy on me, God. People want to swallow me up. They attack and oppress me all day long.
My enemies try to swallow me up all day. So many rise up and fight me in their pride.
When I’m afraid, I put my trust in you.
I praise God for his word. I trust in God and won’t be afraid. What can mere flesh do to me?
All day they twist what I say. Every plan they make is meant to hurt me.
They plot together, hide, and watch every step I take. They’re waiting to take my life.
Will they get away with their wrongdoing? In your anger bring the peoples down, God.
You’ve counted all my wanderings. You keep my tears in your bottle. Haven’t you written them in your book?
When I call out, my enemies will turn back. I know this much: God is for me.
I praise God for his word. I praise the LORD for his word.
I trust God and won’t be afraid. What can anyone do to me?
I owe you the vows I made, God. I’ll bring you offerings of thanks.
You’ve rescued my life from death and kept my feet from falling, so I can walk before God in the light of the living.

For the music director, to the tune of “Do Not Destroy.” A poem by David, when he fled from Saul into the cave. Have mercy on me, God, have mercy on me. I take refuge in you. I’ll shelter in the shadow of your wings until the disaster passes.
I cry out to God Most High, the God who acts on my behalf.
He’ll send help from heaven and save me. He rebukes the one chasing me. Selah. God will send his faithful love and his truth.
I’m surrounded by lions. I lie among people burning with rage, whose teeth are spears and arrows and whose tongues are sharp swords.
Be exalted above the heavens, God! Let your glory rise above the whole earth!
They set a net in my path, and my soul bowed low. They dug a pit in front of me and fell into it themselves. Selah.
My heart is steady, God. My heart is steady. I’ll sing, yes, I’ll sing praises.
Wake up, my glory! Wake up, lute and harp! I’ll wake the dawn.
I’ll thank you, Lord, among the peoples. I’ll sing praises to you among the nations.
Your great faithful love reaches to the heavens, and your truth reaches to the skies.
Be exalted above the heavens, God. Let your glory be over the whole earth.
For the music director, to the tune of “Do Not Destroy.” A poem by David. Do you who stay silent really speak for what is right? Do you people judge fairly?
Deep down you plan injustice. With your hands you deal out violence across the land.
The wicked stray from the womb. From birth they go their own way, spreading lies.
Their venom is like a snake’s, like a deaf cobra that closes its ears,
refusing to hear the snake charmers, however skillfully they play.
God, break the teeth in their mouths. LORD, knock out the fangs of those young lions.
Let them disappear like water running off. When they draw their bows, let their arrows lose their points.
Let them disappear like a snail that melts away, like a stillborn child who never saw the sun.
Before your pots feel the heat of the thorns, he’ll sweep away both the green branches and the burning ones.
Those who do right will rejoice when they see justice done. They’ll wash their feet in the blood of the wicked,
and people will say, “There really is a reward for the righteous. There really is a God who judges the earth.”

For the music director, to the tune of “Do Not Destroy.” A poem by David, when Saul sent men to watch David’s house and kill him. Rescue me from my enemies, my God. Set me out of reach of those who rise against me.
Rescue me from people who do evil. Save me from those who thirst for blood.
Look, they’re lying in wait to take my life. Powerful men gather against me, though I haven’t rebelled or sinned, LORD.
I’ve done nothing wrong, yet they’re ready to attack. Rise up, see what’s happening, and help me!
LORD God of Armies, God of Israel, rise up to punish the nations. Show no mercy to those who betray others and do evil. Selah.
They come back at evening, howling like dogs and prowling around the city.
Listen to what pours out of their mouths. Their words are like swords. “Who can hear us?” they say.
But you laugh at them, LORD. You scoff at all the nations.
My Strength, I watch for you, because God is my fortress.
My God will go ahead of me with his faithful love. He’ll let me look on my enemies in triumph.
Don’t kill them, or my people may forget. Scatter them by your power and bring them down, Lord, our shield.
Let them be caught in their pride because of the sins they speak, the curses and lies on their lips.
Consume them in your wrath until they’re gone. Let them know that God rules over Jacob, to the ends of the earth. Selah.
Let them come back at evening, howling like dogs and roaming the city.
Let them wander in search of food and stay up all night if they can’t get enough.
But I’ll sing about your strength. In the morning I’ll sing aloud about your faithful love, because you’ve been my fortress, a refuge when I was in trouble.
I’ll sing praises to you, my Strength. God is my fortress, the God who shows me mercy.

For the music director, to the tune of “The Lily of the Covenant.” A teaching poem by David, when he fought Aram Naharaim and Aram Zobah and Joab returned and killed twelve thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt. God, you rejected us and broke us down. You were angry. Restore us again.
You shook the land and tore it open. Mend its cracks, because it’s still shaking.
You put your people through hard things. You made us drink wine that left us staggering.
You gave those who fear you a banner to raise for the sake of truth. Selah.
Save us with your right hand and answer us, so the people you love can be rescued.
God has spoken from his sanctuary: “I’ll triumph. I’ll divide Shechem and measure out the valley of Succoth.
Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine. Ephraim is my helmet, and Judah is my scepter.
