Moab is my washbasin. I’ll throw my sandal over Edom. I shout in triumph over Philistia.”
Who will bring me into the fortified city? Who has led me to Edom?
Haven’t you rejected us, God? You no longer march out with our armies.
Help us against the enemy, because human help won’t save us.
With God we’ll fight bravely, because he’ll trample our enemies.
For the music director, with a stringed instrument. By David. Hear my cry, God. Listen to my prayer.
From the ends of the earth I call to you when my heart gives out. Lead me to the rock that stands higher than I can reach.
You’ve been my refuge, a strong tower where my enemy can’t reach me.
I’ll live in your tent forever. I’ll take refuge under the shelter of your wings. Selah.
You’ve heard my vows, God. You’ve given me the inheritance of those who fear your name.
You’ll add days to the king’s life. His years will stretch across generations.
May he sit on his throne before God forever. Send your faithful love and truth to guard him.
Then I’ll sing praise to your name forever and keep my vows day after day.
For the music director. For Jeduthun. A psalm by David. My soul finds rest in God alone. My salvation comes from him.
He alone is my rock, my salvation, and my fortress. I won’t be shaken badly.
How long will all of you attack one person? Would you push him over like a leaning wall or a wobbling fence?
Their whole plan is to pull him down from his high place. They love lies. They bless him out loud and curse him in their hearts. Selah.
My soul, wait quietly for God alone. My hope comes from him.
He alone is my rock and my salvation, my fortress. I won’t be shaken.
My salvation and honor depend on God. God is my strong rock and my refuge.
Trust him at all times, you people. Pour out your hearts before him. God is a refuge for us. Selah.
Ordinary people are only a breath, and people of high standing are an illusion. Put them all on the scales and they rise together, lighter than a breath.
Don’t rely on oppression or put empty hopes in what you steal. If your wealth grows, don’t set your heart on it.
God has spoken once, and twice I’ve heard this: power belongs to God.
Faithful love also belongs to you, Lord, because you repay each person according to what they’ve done.

A psalm by David, when he was in the wilderness of Judah. God, you are my God. I seek you with all my heart. My soul thirsts for you, and my body longs for you in a dry, weary land where there’s no water.
I’ve seen you in the sanctuary and looked on your power and glory.
Your faithful love is better than life, so my lips will praise you.
I’ll bless you as long as I live. I’ll lift my hands in your name.
My soul will be satisfied as if I’d eaten the richest food. I’ll praise you with joyful lips
when I remember you on my bed and think about you through the watches of the night.
You’ve been my help, so I’ll sing for joy in the shadow of your wings.
My soul clings to you, and your right hand holds me up.
Those who want to destroy me will go down into the depths of the earth.
They’ll be handed over to the sword and become food for jackals.
But the king will rejoice in God. Everyone who swears by him will praise him, because the mouths of liars will be shut.
For the music director. A psalm by David. God, hear my voice as I bring you my complaint. Keep me alive through the terror my enemy brings.
Hide me from the plots of the wicked and from the noisy crowd of evildoers.
They sharpen their tongues like swords and aim deadly words like arrows,
to shoot at innocent people from hiding. They strike without warning and without fear.
They urge each other on in their evil plans. They talk about setting traps in secret and say, “Who will see them?”
They plot injustice and say, “We’ve worked out the perfect plan!” The human mind and heart are deep and crafty.
But God will shoot at them. An arrow will strike them without warning.
Their own tongues will bring them down. Everyone who sees them will shake their head.
People everywhere will stand in awe. They’ll tell of God’s work and think carefully about what he’s done.
The righteous will rejoice in the LORD and take refuge in him. Everyone with an upright heart will praise him!
For the music director. A psalm by David. A song. Praise awaits you in Zion, God, and there we’ll keep our vows to you.
You hear prayer. People everywhere will come to you.
Our sins overwhelmed me, but you made atonement for our rebellion.
Blessed are those you choose and bring near to live in your courts. We’ll have our fill of the goodness of your house, your holy temple.
You answer us with righteous deeds that fill us with awe, God who saves us. You’re the hope of those at the ends of the earth and far out at sea.
You set the mountains in place by your power, armed with strength.
You quiet the roar of the seas, the crashing of their waves, and the uproar of the nations.
Even people in distant places stand in awe of your wonders. You make dawn and evening shout for joy.
You come to the earth and water it, making it rich. The river of God is full of water. You provide grain for the people because that’s how you prepared the land.
You soak the furrows and level the ridges. With showers you soften the soil and bless its crops.
You crown the year with your goodness. Your carts spill over with plenty.
The grasslands of the wilderness overflow, and the hills are dressed in joy.
Flocks cover the pastures, and grain clothes the valleys. They shout for joy and sing.
For the music director. A song. A psalm. Shout for joy to God, all the earth!
Sing about the glory of his name. Give him glory and praise!
Say to God, “Your deeds fill us with awe! Your power is so great that your enemies submit to you.
The whole earth will worship you and sing to you. They’ll sing praise to your name.” Selah.
Come and see what God has done, the wonders he’s worked for humanity.
He turned the sea into dry ground, and his people crossed the river on foot. There we rejoiced in him.
He rules by his power forever. He keeps watch over the nations. Let those who rebel against him keep from rising up. Selah.
Praise our God, you peoples! Let everyone hear you praise him.
He keeps us alive and keeps our feet from slipping.
You’ve tested us, God. You’ve refined us like silver.
You brought us into prison and laid heavy loads on our backs.
You let people ride over our heads. We passed through fire and water, but you brought us out to a place of plenty.
I’ll come into your temple with burnt offerings and keep the vows I made to you,
the promises I spoke with my own lips when I was in trouble.
I’ll bring you fat animals as burnt offerings, including rams. I’ll offer bulls and goats. Selah.
Come and listen, all you who fear God. I’ll tell you what he’s done for me.
I cried out to him with my mouth, and my tongue lifted him up in praise.
If I’d held on to sin in my heart, the Lord wouldn’t have listened.
But God did listen. He heard my prayer.
Blessed be God! He received my prayer and kept showing me his faithful love.
For the music director, with stringed instruments. A psalm. A song. May God show us mercy and bless us. May his face shine on us. Selah.
May the earth come to know your way, and every nation know how you save.
Let the peoples praise you, God. Let all the peoples praise you.
Let the nations be glad and sing for joy, because you judge the peoples fairly and guide the nations on earth. Selah.
Let the peoples praise you, God. Let all the peoples praise you.
The earth has given its harvest. God, our own God, will bless us.
God will bless us, and people at the ends of the earth will stand in awe of him.
For the music director. A psalm by David. A song. Let God rise up! Let his enemies scatter and those who hate him run from him!
Drive them away like smoke in the wind. Let the wicked perish before God like wax melting in the fire.
Let the righteous be glad. Let them rejoice before God and celebrate with joy.
Sing to God! Sing praise to his name! Honor the one who rides on the clouds. His name is the LORD. Rejoice before him!
God in his holy dwelling is a father to the fatherless and a defender of widows.
God gives lonely people a family and leads prisoners out singing, while those who rebel live in a land scorched by the sun.
God, when you went out ahead of your people and marched through the wilderness… Selah.
The earth shook and the sky poured down rain before the God of Sinai, before God, the God of Israel.
You sent abundant rain, God. You restored your inheritance when it was worn out.
Your people settled there. In your goodness, God, you provided for the poor.
The Lord gave the word, and a great crowd spread the news.
“Kings and their armies are running! They’re running!” The women at home divide what was taken,
while you rest among the campfires, the wings of a dove covered in silver and its feathers shining with gold.
When the Almighty scattered kings there, snow fell on Zalmon.
The mountains of Bashan are majestic. The mountains of Bashan rise in rugged peaks.
Why do you rugged mountains look with envy at the mountain God chose to rule from? The LORD will live there forever.
God’s chariots number in the tens of thousands, thousands upon thousands. The Lord is among them, coming from Sinai into the sanctuary.
You went up on high and led captives away. You received gifts from people, even from those who rebelled, so that the LORD God might live there.
Blessed be the Lord! Day after day he carries our burdens, the God who saves us. Selah.
Our God is a God who rescues. The Lord GOD has the power to save from death.
God will strike the heads of his enemies, the hairy scalps of those who keep walking in their guilt.
The Lord said, “I’ll bring them back from Bashan. I’ll bring them back from the depths of the sea,
so you can crush them and dip your feet in blood, and your dogs can have their share of your enemies.”
People have seen your procession, God, the procession of my God and King into the sanctuary.
The singers went first. The musicians followed, among young women playing tambourines.
“Bless God in the gatherings. Bless the Lord in the assembly of Israel!”
There’s little Benjamin leading them, the leaders of Judah with their crowd, and the leaders of Zebulun and Naphtali.
Your God has commanded your strength. Show your strength, God, and uphold what you’ve done for us.
Because of your temple in Jerusalem, kings will bring you gifts.
Rebuke the beast among the reeds and the herd of bulls with the calves of the peoples. Trample their bars of silver. Scatter the nations that love war.
Princes will come from Egypt. Ethiopia will hurry to stretch out its hands to God.
Sing to God, kingdoms of the earth! Sing praises to the Lord. Selah.
Sing to the one who rides through the ancient highest heavens. Listen as he raises his mighty voice.
Give God the credit for his strength! His majesty is over Israel, and his power fills the skies.
God, you fill us with awe in your sanctuaries. The God of Israel gives his people strength and power. Praise be to God!
For the music director, to the tune of “Lilies.” By David. Save me, God! The water is up to my neck.
I’m sinking in deep mud with nowhere to plant my feet. I’ve slipped into deep water, and the flood is sweeping over me.
I’m worn out from crying. My throat is dry, and my eyes are tired from looking for my God.
More people hate me for no reason than I have hairs on my head. Powerful enemies want to wipe me out without cause. They make me pay back what I never stole.
God, you know my foolishness. None of my sins are hidden from you.
Lord GOD of Armies, keep those who wait for you from being shamed because of me. God of Israel, keep those who seek you from being dishonored because of me.
I’ve taken insults for your sake, and shame covers my face.
I’ve become a stranger to my brothers, an outsider to my own mother’s children.
My passion for your house consumes me. The insults of those who insult you have fallen on me.
When I wept and fasted, people mocked me for it.
When I put on sackcloth, I became a joke to them.
People sitting at the city gate talk about me, and drunkards sing songs about me.
But I pray to you, LORD, at a time when you are ready to hear. In your abundant faithful love, God, answer me with the rescue you’ve promised.
Pull me out of the mud and keep me from sinking. Rescue me from those who hate me and from the deep water.
Keep the flood from sweeping over me, the depths from swallowing me, and the pit from closing its mouth on me.
Answer me, LORD, because your faithful love is good. Turn toward me in your great compassion.
Don’t hide your face from your servant. I’m in trouble. Answer me quickly!
Come close and redeem my life. Ransom me because of my enemies.
You know the insults I’ve taken, my shame, and my disgrace. You see every one of my enemies.
Their insults broke my heart, and I’m weighed down with grief. I looked for someone to show pity, but no one did. I looked for comfort and found none.
They put poison in my food and gave me vinegar to drink when I was thirsty.
Let the table set before them become a snare, a trap that pays them back.
Let their eyes grow dark so they can’t see, and let their backs stay bent.
Pour out your anger on them. Let the heat of your wrath catch up with them.
Let their homes lie empty. Let no one live in their tents.
They go after the one you’ve wounded and talk about the pain of those you’ve hurt.
Charge them with one wrong after another. Don’t count them among the righteous.
Erase their names from the book of life. Keep them out of the record of the righteous.
I’m in pain and distress. Let your salvation lift me to safety, God.
I’ll praise God’s name with a song and honor him with thanks.
That will please the LORD more than an ox, more than a bull with horns and hooves.
The humble will see and be glad. Let your hearts come alive, you who seek God.
The LORD hears the needy and cares about his people in captivity.
Let heaven and earth praise him, along with the seas and everything that moves in them!
God will save Zion and rebuild the cities of Judah. His people will settle there and make it their own.
The children of his servants will inherit the land. Those who love his name will live there.
For the music director. By David. For remembrance. Hurry, God, to rescue me. Come quickly to help me, LORD.
Let those who want to take my life be put to shame and confusion. Turn back in disgrace those who want to see me ruined.
Let the ones who say, “Aha! Aha!” turn away in shame.
Let all who seek you rejoice and be glad in you. Let those who love your salvation keep saying, “Let God be exalted!”
I’m poor and needy. Come quickly, God. You’re my help and my rescuer. LORD, don’t delay.
LORD, I take refuge in you. Never let me be put to shame.
In your righteousness, come to my rescue. Bend down to hear me and save me.
Be my rock of refuge, somewhere I can always go. Give the order to save me, because you’re my rock and my fortress.
Rescue me, my God, from the grip of the wicked, from people who do wrong and act cruelly.
You are my hope, Lord GOD. I’ve trusted you since I was young.
I’ve depended on you since before I was born. You brought me out of my mother’s womb. I’ll always praise you.
Many people look at me in wonder, but you are my strong refuge.
My mouth is full of your praise and speaks of your honor all day long.
Don’t cast me aside in my old age. Don’t leave me when my strength gives out.
My enemies talk about me. The ones waiting to take my life make plans together,
saying, “God has left him. Chase him and catch him, because no one will rescue him.”
God, stay close to me. My God, hurry to help me.
Let my accusers be put to shame and brought to an end. Cover those who want to hurt me with disgrace and scorn.
I’ll keep hoping in you and give you more and more praise.
I’ll speak of your righteousness and your salvation all day long, even though I can’t take in how great they are.
I’ll come telling the mighty acts of the Lord GOD. I’ll speak of your righteousness, yours alone.
God, you’ve taught me since I was young. To this day I’ve told people what wonders you’ve done.
Even when I’m old and gray, God, stay with me until I’ve told the next generation about your strength and everyone yet to come about your power.
Your righteousness reaches to the heavens, God. You’ve done great things. Who is like you?
You’ve made us see many bitter troubles, but you’ll give me life again. You’ll bring us up from the depths of the earth.
Restore my honor and comfort me again.
I’ll praise you with the harp for your faithfulness, my God. I’ll sing to you with the lyre, Holy One of Israel.
My lips will shout for joy! My soul, which you’ve redeemed, will sing your praise.
I’ll tell of your righteousness all day long, because those who wanted to harm me have been put to shame and confusion.
By Solomon. God, give the king your sense of justice and give your righteousness to the king’s son.
He’ll judge your people with righteousness and give the poor the justice they deserve.
May the mountains bring the people prosperity and the hills yield the fruit of righteousness.
May he defend the poor, save the children of those in need, and crush the oppressor.
May people fear you as long as the sun and moon endure, through every generation.
May the king come down like rain on freshly cut grass, like showers watering the earth.
In his days may the righteous flourish and peace abound until the moon is gone.
May he rule from sea to sea, from the River to the ends of the earth.
May those who live in the wilderness bow before him and his enemies lick the dust.
May the kings of Tarshish and the islands bring tribute, and the kings of Sheba and Seba bring gifts.
May every king bow before him and every nation serve him.
He’ll rescue the needy when they cry out, and the poor who have no one to help.
He’ll have compassion on the poor and needy, and he’ll save the lives of those in need.
He’ll rescue them from oppression and violence. Their blood will be precious to him.
May he live long and receive gold from Sheba. May people pray for him continually and bless him all day long.
May grain grow in abundance throughout the land. May its fruit sway like Lebanon and flourish like grass in the fields.
May his name last forever, as long as the sun shines. May people find blessing through him and all nations call him blessed.
Praise the LORD God, the God of Israel. He alone does wonderful things.
Bless his glorious name forever! Let the whole earth be filled with his glory! Amen and amen.
This ends the prayers of David son of Jesse.
A psalm by Asaph. God really is good to Israel, to those whose hearts are pure.
Me? I almost lost my footing. One more step and I would’ve slipped.
I envied the arrogant when I saw how well the wicked had it.
They don’t struggle when death comes. Their strength holds up.
They don’t carry the burdens other people do. The troubles that hit everyone else seem to pass them by.
So they wear pride like a necklace and violence like an outfit.
Their eyes bulge with fat. Their minds run wild with conceit.
They mock people and talk with malice. They throw their weight around and threaten to crush others.
They aim their mouths at heaven, and their tongues roam the whole earth.
So their people keep coming back to them and drink it all in like water.
They say, “How would God know? Does the Most High even know what’s going on?”
Look at the wicked. They’re always taking it easy, and their wealth keeps piling up.
Was all that work to keep my heart clean and my hands innocent for nothing?
Trouble hits me all day long, and every morning feels like another punishment.
If I’d said, “I’m going to talk like them,” I would’ve betrayed a whole generation of your children.
I tried to make sense of it, but it hurt too much to think about
until I stepped into God’s sanctuary and saw where their road ends.
You really do set them on slippery ground. You send them crashing into ruin.
Just like that, they’re destroyed, swept away in terror.
They’re like a dream when someone wakes up. When you rise, Lord, you’ll treat their illusions with contempt.
My soul was hurting, and bitterness had settled deep in my heart.
I was clueless and didn’t understand. Before you, I was acting like a wild animal.
And still, I’m here with you. You’ve got hold of my right hand.
You’ll guide me with your counsel, then welcome me into glory.
Who else do I have in heaven? There’s no one on earth I want more than you.
My body and my heart may give out, but God is the strength of my heart and my share forever.
Anyone who stays far from you will perish. You destroy everyone who turns away from you in unfaithfulness.
As for me, being close to God is good. I’ve made the Lord GOD my safe place so I can tell people everything you’ve done.
A psalm for reflection by Asaph. God, why have you pushed us away for good? Why is your anger still smoldering against the sheep of your own pasture?
Remember the people you bought long ago, the tribe you rescued to be your own. Remember Mount Zion, where you made your home.
Come walk through these ruins that never seem to end. Look at all the damage the enemy did in your sanctuary.
Your enemies roared right in the middle of your gathering place. They put up their own banners as signs.
They went at it like people swinging axes through a thicket.
They smashed all the carved woodwork with hatchets and hammers.
They burned your sanctuary to the ground. They defiled the place where your name dwells.
They said to themselves, “We’ll crush them completely.” They burned every place in the land where people worshiped God.
We don’t see any miraculous signs. There’s no prophet left, and nobody here knows how long this will last.
How long will the enemy mock you, God? Will they drag your name through the dirt forever?
Why are you holding back your hand, your right hand? Pull it out from against your chest and finish them!
Yet you’ve been my King from long ago, God, bringing rescue all across the earth.
You split the sea by your strength. You smashed the heads of the sea monsters in the water.
You shattered Leviathan’s heads and gave him as food to people and creatures in the desert.
You opened up springs and streams. You dried up mighty rivers.
The day is yours, and so is the night. You put the light and the sun in place.
You set every boundary of the earth. You made summer and winter.
Remember how the enemy mocked you, LORD. Foolish people have insulted your name.
Don’t hand your dove over to wild beasts. Don’t forget the lives of your poor forever.
Honor your covenant. The dark places of the earth are full of hideouts where violence thrives.
Don’t send the oppressed away in shame. Let the poor and needy praise your name.
Rise up, God! Stand up for your own cause. Remember how fools mock you all day long.
Don’t forget the voices of your enemies. The roar of those who rise against you never lets up.
For the music director, to the tune of “Do Not Destroy.” A psalm by Asaph. A song. Thank you, God! We thank you because your name is near. People tell stories of the wonders you’ve done.
“When I decide the time has come, I’ll judge fairly.
The earth shakes, and everyone on it trembles. I’m the one who holds its pillars steady.” Selah.
I told the arrogant, “Quit bragging!” I told the wicked, “Keep your horns down.
Don’t raise your horns high or talk with your necks stiff and proud.”
Being lifted up doesn’t come from the east, the west, or the south.
God is the judge. He brings one person down and lifts another up.
The LORD holds a cup of foaming wine mixed with spices. He pours it out, and the wicked of the earth drink it down to the last drop.
As for me, I’ll keep telling this forever. I’ll sing praise to the God of Jacob.
“I’ll cut off every horn of the wicked, but the horns of the righteous will be raised high.”
For the music director, with stringed instruments. A psalm by Asaph. A song. People know God in Judah. His name is great in Israel.
His tent is in Salem, and his home is in Zion.
That’s where he broke the flaming arrows, the shield, the sword, and the weapons of war. Selah.
You shine with glory, more majestic than mountains full of prey.
The bravest warriors lie stripped of what they had. They’ve fallen into their last sleep. None of them can lift a hand.
At your rebuke, God of Jacob, horse and chariot alike fall still in the sleep of death.
You’re the one to fear. When you’re angry, who can stand before you?
You handed down your judgment from heaven. The earth trembled and went quiet
when you rose to judge, God, to save everyone on earth who was suffering. Selah.
Even human anger ends up bringing you praise. You hold back those who survive your wrath.
Make your vows to the LORD your God and keep them! Let everyone around him bring gifts to the one who fills them with awe.
He breaks the spirit of rulers. Even the kings of the earth fear him.
For the music director. For Jeduthun. A psalm by Asaph. I cry out to God! I call on him for help, asking him to hear me.
When trouble hit, I looked for the Lord. I kept my hand stretched out through the night and didn’t let it drop. My soul wouldn’t be comforted.
I think of God and groan. I voice my pain, and my spirit feels overwhelmed. Selah.
You keep my eyes wide open. I’m so upset I can’t even speak.
I think back to the old days, to years long gone.
At night I remember my song. I search my heart, and my spirit keeps asking:
“Will the Lord turn us away forever? Will he never show us favor again?
Has his faithful love disappeared for good? Has his promise failed for every generation to come?
Has God forgotten how to show grace? Has anger made him hold back his compassion?” Selah.
Then I thought, “Here’s where I’ll turn: to those years when the Most High showed the power of his right hand.”
I’ll remember what the LORD has done. I’ll remember your wonders from long ago.
I’ll think deeply about all your work and turn over in my mind what you’ve done.
God, your way is in the sanctuary. What god is as great as you?
You’re the God who works wonders. You’ve shown your strength among the peoples.
With your own arm you redeemed your people, the descendants of Jacob and Joseph. Selah.
The waters saw you, God. They saw you and twisted in fear. Even the depths shook.
The clouds poured out water. Thunder rolled through the skies, and your arrows flashed all around.
Your thunder roared in the whirlwind. Lightning lit up the world, and the earth shook and trembled.
Your road ran through the sea. Your paths crossed the mighty waters, yet no one saw your footprints.
You led your people like a flock, with Moses and Aaron to guide them.
A psalm for reflection by Asaph. Listen to what I’m teaching you, my people. Lean in and hear what I’m saying.
I’ll tell you a parable and speak the hard-to-understand sayings from long ago,
things we’ve heard and known because our ancestors told us.
We won’t keep them from their children. We’ll tell the next generation what makes the LORD worthy of praise, how strong he is, and what wonders he’s done.
He established a covenant in Jacob and gave Israel his teaching. He told our ancestors to pass it on to their children,
so the next generation would know it, even the children who weren’t born yet. Then they’d grow up and tell their own children.
That way they’d put their hope in God, remember what he’s done, and keep his commands.
They wouldn’t turn out like their ancestors, stubborn and rebellious, with hearts that wouldn’t stay loyal and spirits that wouldn’t stick with God.
Ephraim’s people had their bows ready, but when battle came, they turned back.
They broke God’s covenant and refused to live by his instruction.
They forgot what he’d done and all the wonders he’d shown them.
He did amazing things right in front of their ancestors in Egypt, in the fields of Zoan.
He split the sea and led them through it. He piled up the water so it stood in place.
By day he led them with a cloud. All night he led them with the light of fire.
He split rocks in the wilderness and gave them water like it was pouring from the depths.
He made streams gush out of the rock, and water ran down like rivers.
Still they kept sinning against him and rebelling against the Most High in the desert.
In their hearts they put God to the test by demanding the food they craved.
They talked against God and said, “Can God spread a table out here in the wilderness?
Sure, he struck the rock and water gushed out until streams overflowed. But can he give us bread too? Can he give his people meat?”
The LORD heard them and was furious. A fire flared up against Jacob, and anger rose against Israel,
because they didn’t believe God or trust him to save them.
Even so, he gave orders to the skies above and opened heaven’s doors.
He rained down manna for them to eat. He gave them food from the sky.
People ate the bread of angels. He sent them all the food they could eat.
He made the east wind blow across the sky and steered the south wind by his power.
He rained meat down like dust, birds as countless as sand by the sea.
He dropped them right in the middle of the camp, all around their homes.
The people ate until they were full. He gave them what they craved.
They still hadn’t let go of their cravings. The food was still in their mouths
when God’s anger rose against them. He killed some of their strongest and struck down Israel’s young men.
After all that, they still sinned and refused to believe in his wonders.
So he let their days come to nothing and their years pass in terror.
When he struck them down, they started looking for him. They turned back and sought God in earnest.
They remembered that God was their rock, that God Most High was the one who redeemed them.
But they just tried to flatter him. The words on their tongues were lies.
Their hearts weren’t right with him, and they didn’t stay faithful to his covenant.
But he had mercy. He forgave their wrongdoing and spared them. Again and again he turned his anger away and held back the full force of his wrath.
He remembered they were only flesh, like a gust of wind that passes and never comes back.
How often they rebelled against him in the wilderness and caused him grief in the desert!
Again they put God to the test and provoked the Holy One of Israel.
They forgot the power of his hand and the day he rescued them from their enemy.
They forgot the signs he performed in Egypt and the wonders he showed in the fields of Zoan.
He turned their rivers and streams into blood, so they couldn’t drink from them.
He sent swarms of flies that devoured them and frogs that brought ruin.
He gave their crops to caterpillars and everything they’d worked for to locusts.
He wrecked their vines with hail and their sycamore fig trees with frost.
He handed their livestock over to the hail and their flocks to blazing thunderbolts.
He unleashed the full heat of his anger on them, wrath, indignation, and trouble, with a band of angels bringing disaster.
He cleared a path for his anger. He didn’t spare their lives from death. He handed them over to plague.
He struck down every firstborn in Egypt, the first of their strength in the tents of Ham.
But he led his own people out like sheep and guided them through the wilderness like a flock.
He led them safely, so they had no reason to fear. The sea swept over their enemies.
He brought them to the edge of his holy land, to this mountain his right hand had won.
He drove out the nations ahead of them, measured out their inheritance, and settled the tribes of Israel in their tents.
Still they tested and rebelled against God Most High. They refused to keep his commands.
They turned back and betrayed him like their ancestors. They were as unreliable as a warped bow.
They angered him with their high places and stirred up his jealousy with their carved idols.
God heard and was furious. He rejected Israel outright.
He left the tent at Shiloh, the tent he’d set up among people.
He let his strength be taken captive and handed his glory over to the enemy.
He handed his people over to the sword. He was angry with his own inheritance.
Fire devoured their young men, and their young women had no wedding songs.
Their priests fell by the sword, and their widows couldn’t even weep.
Then the Lord rose like someone waking from sleep, like a warrior shouting after drinking wine.
He struck his enemies and drove them back, putting them to shame forever.
He rejected Joseph’s tent and passed over the tribe of Ephraim.
He chose the tribe of Judah and Mount Zion, which he loved.
He built his sanctuary high like the heavens, firm like the earth he’s established forever.
He chose David as his servant and took him from the sheep pens.
He called him away from tending sheep with their lambs to shepherd Jacob, his people, and Israel, his inheritance.
David shepherded them with an honest heart and guided them with skillful hands.
A psalm by Asaph. God, the nations have invaded what belongs to you. They’ve defiled your holy temple and left Jerusalem in piles of rubble.
They’ve left your servants’ bodies for the birds to eat and the flesh of your faithful people for wild animals.
They’ve poured out blood like water all around Jerusalem. Nobody was left to bury the dead.
We’ve become a disgrace to our neighbors. Everyone around us laughs and mocks us.
How long, LORD? Will you stay angry forever? Will your jealousy keep burning like fire?
Pour out your wrath on nations that don’t know you and kingdoms that never call on your name.
They’ve devoured Jacob and wrecked his homeland.
Don’t hold our ancestors’ wrongs against us. Let your tender mercy reach us quickly. We’re desperate.
Help us, God who saves us, for the glory of your name. Rescue us and forgive our sins for the sake of your name.
Why should the nations get to say, “Where’s their God?” Let them see, right in front of us, that you’re avenging your servants’ blood.
Let the prisoners’ groans reach you. Use your great power to save those sentenced to die.
Lord, pay our neighbors back seven times over for the insults they threw at you.
Then we, your people, the sheep of your pasture, will thank you forever. We’ll tell every generation why you deserve praise.
For the music director, to the tune of “The Lilies of the Covenant.” A psalm by Asaph. Hear us, Shepherd of Israel. You lead Joseph like a flock. You sit above the cherubim. Shine out!
Show your strength before Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasseh. Come save us!
Bring us back, God. Let your face shine on us, and we’ll be saved.
LORD God of Armies, how long will your anger burn against your people’s prayers?
You’ve fed them bread made of tears and given them tears to drink by the bowlful.
You’ve made our neighbors fight over us, and our enemies laugh among themselves.
Bring us back, God of Armies. Let your face shine on us, and we’ll be saved.
You brought a vine out of Egypt. You drove out the nations and planted it.
You cleared the ground for it. It sank its roots deep and filled the land.
Its shade covered the mountains, and its branches were like God’s cedars.
It spread its branches all the way to the sea and sent its shoots out to the River.
Why did you break down its walls so anyone walking by can pick from it?
Wild boars from the woods tear it up, and animals from the fields feed on it.
Come back, God of Armies, please. Look down from heaven. See what’s happened and come care for this vine,
the root your right hand planted, the branch you made strong for yourself.
It’s been burned and cut down. At your rebuke they perish.
Let your hand rest on the man at your right hand, the son of man you made strong for yourself.
Then we won’t turn away from you. Bring us back to life and we’ll call on your name.
Bring us back, LORD God of Armies. Let your face shine on us, and we’ll be saved.
For the music director, on an instrument from Gath. By Asaph. Sing out to God, our strength! Give a joyful shout to the God of Jacob!
Start the song. Bring the tambourine, the sweet-sounding lyre, and the harp.
Sound the trumpet at the new moon and at the full moon, on our feast day.
That’s a rule for Israel, an instruction from the God of Jacob.
He made it a covenant for Joseph when he went out over Egypt. I heard a language I didn’t know.
“I lifted the load off his shoulder. I freed his hands from the basket.
You cried out when trouble hit, and I rescued you. I answered you from the hidden place of thunder. I tested you at the waters of Meribah.” Selah.
“Listen, my people. I have a warning for you. Israel, if only you’d hear me out!
Keep foreign gods out of your midst. Don’t bow down to any of them.
I’m the LORD your God. I brought you up out of Egypt. Open your mouth wide, and I’ll fill it.
But my people didn’t listen to me. Israel wanted nothing to do with me.
So I let them follow their stubborn hearts and go wherever their own plans took them.
If only my people would listen to me! If only Israel would walk in my ways!
I’d bring their enemies down in no time and turn my hand against those who oppose them.
Those who hate the LORD would cower before him, and their punishment would last forever.
But he would feed his people the finest wheat. I’d give you honey from the rock until you’d had your fill.”
A psalm by Asaph. God takes his place in the great assembly. He hands down judgment among the gods.
“How long are you going to twist justice and take the side of the wicked?” Selah.
“Stand up for the weak, the poor, and the fatherless. Defend the rights of those who are poor and pushed around.
Rescue the weak and needy. Pull them out of the grip of the wicked.”
They have no clue and don’t understand. They go back and forth in the dark, and every foundation of the earth shakes.
I said, “You’re gods, every one of you a son of the Most High.
Even so, you’ll die like mortals and fall like any other ruler.”
Rise up, God, and judge the earth. Every nation is yours to inherit.
A song. A psalm by Asaph. God, don’t stay silent. Don’t go quiet or stand still, God.
Look, your enemies are making noise. The people who hate you are raising their heads.
They’re scheming against your people and plotting against the ones you love.
“Come on,” they say, “let’s wipe them out as a nation, so nobody remembers the name Israel.”
They’ve all agreed on a plan. They’ve teamed up against you:
the people in Edom’s tents and the Ishmaelites, Moab and the Hagrites,
Gebal, Ammon, and Amalek, Philistia and the people of Tyre.
Even Assyria has joined them and backed up Lot’s descendants. Selah.
Do to them what you did to Midian, and what you did to Sisera and Jabin at the Kishon River.
They died at Endor and became like manure on the ground.
Make their nobles end up like Oreb and Zeeb, and all their rulers like Zebah and Zalmunna,
who said, “Let’s take God’s pasturelands for ourselves.”
My God, send them rolling like tumbleweed, blowing like chaff in the wind.
Like fire burning through a forest, like flames setting mountains ablaze,
chase them down with your tempest and terrify them with your storm.
Let confusion cover their faces so they’ll seek your name, LORD.
Let them be put to shame and terrified forever. Let them be bewildered and perish,
so they’ll know that you alone, whose name is the LORD, are Most High over the whole earth.
For the music director, on an instrument from Gath. A psalm by the sons of Korah. What a beautiful place you live in, LORD of Armies!
I’m aching to be in the LORD’s courts. My heart and my whole body cry out for the living God.
Even a sparrow has found a home, and a swallow has built a nest for her young near your altars, LORD of Armies, my King and my God.
Blessed are those who live in your house. They never stop praising you. Selah.
Blessed are those who get their strength from you and set their hearts on the journey to your house.
When they pass through the Valley of Weeping, they turn it into a place of springs. The autumn rain covers it with blessings.
They grow stronger as they go, until every one of them stands before God in Zion.
LORD God of Armies, hear my prayer. Listen to me, God of Jacob. Selah.
God, our shield, look with favor on the face of your anointed one.
One day in your courts beats a thousand anywhere else. I’d rather stand at the door of my God’s house than live in the tents of the wicked.
The LORD God is a sun and a shield. The LORD gives grace and glory. He holds back nothing good from those who live with integrity.
LORD of Armies, blessed is anyone who trusts you.
For the music director. A psalm by the sons of Korah. LORD, you’ve been good to your land. You’ve restored Jacob’s fortunes.
You forgave your people for what they did wrong and covered all their sin. Selah.
You took away all your wrath and turned back from your burning anger.
Bring us back, God who saves us. Let your anger toward us come to an end.
Will you stay angry with us forever? Will your anger stretch on through every generation?
Won’t you bring us back to life again so your people can rejoice in you?
Show us your faithful love, LORD. Give us your salvation.
I’ll listen to what the LORD God says. He’ll speak peace to his faithful people. Let them stay away from their old foolish ways.
His salvation is close to those who fear him, so glory can make its home in our land.
Mercy and truth meet. Righteousness and peace kiss.
Truth sprouts from the earth, and righteousness looks down from heaven.
The LORD will give what is good, and our land will bring in its harvest.
Righteousness goes ahead of him, clearing the way for his steps.
A prayer by David. LORD, lean in and answer me. I’m poor and in need.
Keep me alive, because I’m faithful to you. You’re my God. Save your servant who trusts you.
Have mercy on me, Lord. I’m calling out to you all day long.
Bring joy back to your servant’s soul, because I lift my whole life up to you, Lord.
You’re good, Lord, and ready to forgive. Your faithful love overflows for everyone who calls on you.
LORD, hear my prayer. Listen to my pleas for help.
When trouble hits, I’ll call on you, because you’ll answer me.
No god is like you, Lord. Nobody does what you do.
Every nation you made will come and worship before you, Lord. They’ll give glory to your name.
You are great and do amazing things. You alone are God.
Teach me your way, LORD, and I’ll walk in your truth. Give me a heart that’s all in when it comes to honoring your name.
I’ll praise you with my whole heart, Lord my God. I’ll give glory to your name forever.
Your faithful love for me is so great. You rescued my life from the deepest part of Sheol.
God, arrogant people have risen against me. A violent mob wants me dead, and they don’t give you a second thought.
But you, Lord, are a God full of mercy and grace. You’re slow to anger and overflowing with faithful love and truth.
Turn toward me and have mercy on me! Give your strength to your servant. Save me, the son of your servant.
Give me a sign of your goodness, so those who hate me will see it and be put to shame. You, LORD, have helped me and comforted me.
A psalm by the sons of Korah. A song. God laid his foundation in the holy mountains.
The LORD loves Zion’s gates more than anywhere else Jacob’s people live.
City of God, people say glorious things about you! Selah.
“I’ll count Rahab and Babylon among those who know me. Look at Philistia, Tyre, and Ethiopia. I’ll say, ‘This one was born there.’”
People will say of Zion, “This one was born here, and so was that one.” The Most High himself will keep the city standing.
When the LORD writes down the names of the peoples, he’ll mark down, “This one was born there.” Selah.
Singers and dancers alike say, “All my springs are in you.”

A song. A psalm by the sons of Korah. For the music director, to the tune of “The Suffering of Affliction.” A psalm for reflection by Heman the Ezrahite. LORD, God who saves me, I’ve cried out to you day and night.
Let my prayer reach you. Lean in and hear my cry.
My soul is packed with trouble, and my life is getting close to Sheol.
People count me among those going down to the pit. I’m like someone with no one to help,
left among the dead, like those killed and laid in the grave, whom you no longer remember. They’re cut off from your hand.
You’ve put me in the lowest pit, down in the deepest dark.
Your anger weighs hard on me. You’ve battered me with wave after wave. Selah.
You’ve driven my friends away and made them recoil from me. I’m shut in and can’t get out.
My eyes are worn out from grief. I call to you every day, LORD, with my hands stretched out to you.
Do you work wonders for the dead? Do the spirits of those who’ve died get up and praise you? Selah.
Does anyone tell of your faithful love in the grave or talk about your faithfulness in Destruction?
Are your wonders known in the dark or your righteousness in the land where everyone is forgotten?
But I’m still crying out to you, LORD. In the morning my prayer comes before you.
LORD, why do you turn my soul away? Why do you hide your face from me?
I’ve suffered and come close to death since I was young. Your terrors leave me beside myself.
Your fierce anger has swept over me. Your terrors have cut me off.
They surround me like floodwater all day long. They’ve swallowed me up.
You’ve put my loved ones and friends far from me, and my friends are lost in the dark.
A psalm for reflection by Ethan the Ezrahite. I’ll sing of the LORD’s faithful love forever. I’ll tell every generation how faithful you are.
Here’s what I say: “Your love stands firm forever. You set the heavens in place, and your faithfulness is there.”
“I made a covenant with the one I chose. I swore to David my servant,
‘I’ll establish your descendants forever and keep your throne standing through every generation.’” Selah.
The heavens praise your wonders, LORD. The holy ones gathered there praise your faithfulness.
Who in the skies can compare to the LORD? Who among the heavenly beings is like him?
God fills the council of the holy ones with awe. Everyone around him fears him above all.
LORD God of Armies, who has power like yours? LORD, your faithfulness surrounds you.
You rule the raging sea. When its waves rise up, you calm them down.
You smashed Rahab and left it like one of the slain. With your mighty arm you scattered your enemies.
The heavens are yours. So is the earth. You laid the foundation of the world and everything in it.
You made north and south. Tabor and Hermon sing for joy at your name.
Your arm is mighty. Your hand is strong, and your right hand is lifted high.
Your throne rests on righteousness and justice. Faithful love and truth go ahead of you.
Blessed are the people who know how to shout your praise. They walk in the light of your presence, LORD.
They rejoice in your name all day long. Your righteousness lifts them up.
You’re the glory behind their strength. Your favor lifts our horn high.
Our shield belongs to the LORD, and our king belongs to the Holy One of Israel.
Then you spoke to your faithful ones in a vision: “I’ve given strength to a warrior. I’ve raised up a young man from among the people.
I found David my servant and anointed him with my holy oil.
My hand will hold him steady. My arm will make him strong.
No enemy will squeeze tribute out of him. No wicked person will oppress him.
I’ll crush his enemies in front of him and strike down those who hate him.
My faithfulness and faithful love will stay with him, and in my name his horn will rise high.
I’ll set his hand over the sea and his right hand over the rivers.
He’ll call out to me, ‘You’re my Father, my God, and the rock that saves me!’
I’ll make him my firstborn, the highest of all the kings of the earth.
I’ll keep showing him faithful love forever. My covenant with him will stand firm.
I’ll make his descendants last forever and his throne last as long as heaven.
If his children abandon my instruction and stop living by my judgments,
if they break my laws and refuse to keep my commands,
I’ll punish their rebellion with the rod and their wrongdoing with blows.
But I won’t take my faithful love away from him or let my faithfulness fail.
I won’t break my covenant or change a word I’ve spoken.
I’ve sworn once by my holiness. I won’t lie to David.
His descendants will last forever. His throne will stand before me like the sun.
It’ll stand forever like the moon, the faithful witness in the sky.” Selah.
But you’ve turned away and rejected your anointed king. You’ve been angry with him.
You’ve renounced your covenant with your servant and dragged his crown through the dust.
You’ve broken down all his defenses and left his strongholds in ruins.
Everyone passing by takes what they want from him. His neighbors mock him.
You’ve lifted up the right hand of his foes and given all his enemies reason to celebrate.
You’ve turned back the edge of his sword and left him without support in battle.
You’ve put an end to his splendor and thrown his throne to the ground.
You’ve cut his youth short and covered him with shame. Selah.
How long, LORD? Will you hide forever? Will your anger keep burning like fire?
Remember how little time I have. How fleeting you’ve made every human life!
Who can live without seeing death? Who can pull their own life out of Sheol’s grip? Selah.
Lord, where is the faithful love you showed before, the love you swore to David in your faithfulness?
Remember the insults your servants have taken, Lord. I carry the taunts of so many powerful peoples in my heart.
Your enemies mock you, LORD. They mock every step your anointed one takes.
Blessed be the LORD forever. Amen and amen.
A prayer by Moses, the man of God. Lord, you’ve been our home through every generation.
Before the mountains were born, before you shaped the earth and the world, you were God. From forever to forever, you are God.
You turn people back to dust and say, “Return, you children of humanity.”
A thousand years to you are like yesterday once it’s gone, like one watch in the night.
You sweep people away while they sleep. In the morning they spring up like fresh grass.
In the morning it sprouts and grows. By evening it’s wilted and dry.
Your anger consumes us. Your wrath leaves us shaken.
You’ve set our wrongs in front of you, even our secret sins in the light of your presence.
All our days slip away under your wrath. Our years end with a sigh.
We get seventy years, maybe eighty if we’re strong. Even the best of them are full of hard work and sorrow. They pass in a flash, and we fly away.
Who really knows the power of your anger? Your wrath is as great as the reverence we owe you.
Teach us to count our days so we can grow wise at heart.
Turn back to us, LORD! How long will it be? Have compassion on your servants!
Fill us in the morning with your faithful love, so we can sing for joy and be glad all our days.
Give us as many days of joy as the days you made us suffer, as many years as we’ve seen trouble.
Let your servants see what you do, and let their children see your glory.
Let the favor of the Lord our God rest on us. Make the work of our hands last. Yes, make the work of our hands last.
Whoever lives in the shelter of the Most High will find rest in the Almighty’s shadow.
I’ll say of the LORD, “He’s my refuge and my fortress. He’s my God, and I trust him.”
He’ll pull you out of the bird catcher’s trap and save you from deadly disease.
He’ll cover you with his feathers, and you’ll find shelter under his wings. His faithfulness is your shield and your defense.
You won’t fear what comes at you in the night or the arrow that flies in broad daylight,
the disease that moves through the dark or the destruction that strikes at noon.
A thousand may fall beside you, ten thousand at your right hand, but it won’t come near you.
You’ll see it with your own eyes when the wicked get what they’ve earned.
You’ve made the LORD your refuge and the Most High your home.
No harm will come to you, and no plague will come near where you live.
He’ll give his angels orders to guard you wherever you go.
They’ll lift you up in their hands so you don’t strike your foot against a stone.
You’ll step on the lion and the cobra. You’ll trample the young lion and the snake underfoot.
“Because he loves me, I’ll rescue him. I’ll lift him out of danger because he knows my name.
He’ll call to me and I’ll answer. I’ll be right there with him in trouble. I’ll rescue him and honor him.
I’ll give him a long life to satisfy him, and I’ll show him how I save.”
A psalm. A song for the Sabbath day. It’s good to thank the LORD and sing praise to your name, Most High,
to tell of your faithful love in the morning and your faithfulness every night,
with the ten-stringed lute, the harp, and the melody of the lyre.
What you’ve done fills me with joy, LORD. I’ll celebrate what your hands have made.
LORD, your works are amazing! Your thoughts go so deep.
People with no sense miss it. Fools can’t get their heads around this:
the wicked may pop up like grass and those who do evil may thrive, but they’ll be destroyed forever.
You, LORD, are on high forever.
Look, LORD, your enemies will perish. Every one of those evildoers will scatter.
But you’ve lifted my horn high like a wild ox’s. You’ve anointed me with fresh oil.
I’ve seen my enemies with my own eyes, and I’ve heard about the wicked who rise up against me.
The righteous will flourish like palm trees and grow tall like cedars in Lebanon.
Planted in the LORD’s house, they’ll flourish in the courts of our God.
Even in old age they’ll still bear fruit. They’ll stay green and full of sap,
showing that the LORD is upright. He’s my rock, and there’s no wrong in him.
The LORD reigns! He wears majesty like a robe and straps on strength. The world is firmly in place. Nothing can move it.
Your throne has stood since long ago. You’ve been here from everlasting.
The floods have risen, LORD. The floods have raised their roar. The floods lift their waves.
Louder than the roar of mighty waters, stronger than the crashing waves of the sea, the LORD on high is mighty.
Your laws stand firm. Holiness makes your house beautiful, LORD, forever.
LORD, you’re the God who brings vengeance. God who brings vengeance, shine out!
Rise up, Judge of the earth. Give the proud what they’ve earned.
How long, LORD? How long will the wicked keep winning?
Arrogant words pour out of their mouths. Everyone doing evil brags about it.
They crush your people, LORD. They make life miserable for those who belong to you.
They kill widows and foreigners and murder children who have no father.
They say, “The LORD won’t see it. Jacob’s God won’t even notice.”
Think about it, you people with no sense. When are you going to wise up?
The one who made the ear can hear, can’t he? The one who formed the eye can see, can’t he?
The one who disciplines nations can hold you accountable, can’t he? The one who teaches humanity knows.
The LORD knows what people think. He knows how empty their plans are.
Blessed are the people you discipline, LORD, and teach from your law,
giving them relief in hard times until the pit is dug for the wicked.
The LORD won’t cast off his people or walk away from his inheritance.
Judgment will line up with righteousness again, and everyone with an upright heart will follow it.
Who’ll stand up for me against the wicked? Who’ll take my side against those who do evil?
If the LORD hadn’t helped me, I would’ve gone down to where all is silent.
When I cried, “I’m losing my footing!” your faithful love held me up, LORD.
When worries crowd my mind, your comfort lifts my spirits.
Could a corrupt throne be on your side when it uses the law to cause harm?
They band together against the righteous and sentence innocent people to death.
But the LORD has been my fortress. My God is the rock where I take refuge.
He turns their own wrongdoing back on them. He’ll put an end to them for their evil. The LORD our God will put an end to them.
Come on, let’s sing to the LORD! Let’s shout for joy to the rock who saves us!
Let’s come into his presence with thanks and lift him up with songs!
The LORD is a great God, a great King above every god.
He holds the deepest places of the earth in his hand. The mountain peaks are his too.
The sea belongs to him because he made it. His hands shaped the dry land.
Come, let’s bow down and worship. Let’s kneel before the LORD who made us.
He’s our God. We’re the people of his pasture, the sheep he takes care of. If only you’d listen to his voice today!
“Don’t harden your hearts like you did at Meribah, like that day at Massah in the wilderness,
when your ancestors put me to the test, even though they saw what I did.
For forty long years that generation grieved me. I said, ‘Their hearts keep going off course. They haven’t learned my ways.’
So I swore in my anger, ‘They’ll never enter my rest.’”
Sing the LORD a new song! Sing to the LORD, everyone on earth!
Sing to the LORD and bless his name! Day after day, tell people how he saves.
Tell the nations about his glory. Let every people hear what wonders he’s done.
The LORD is great and deserves all that praise! He’s to be feared above every god.
The gods of the nations are idols, but the LORD made the heavens.
Honor and majesty stand before him. Strength and beauty fill his sanctuary.
Give the LORD glory and strength, you families of the nations. Give him the credit he deserves.
Give the LORD the glory his name deserves. Bring an offering and come into his courts.
Worship the LORD in holy splendor. Tremble before him, all the earth.
Tell the nations, “The LORD reigns!” The world stands firm. It won’t be moved. He’ll judge the peoples fairly.
Let the heavens be glad and the earth rejoice. Let the sea roar with everything in it!
Let the fields and everything in them celebrate! Then every tree in the woods will sing for joy
before the LORD, because he’s coming. He’s coming to judge the earth. He’ll judge the world with righteousness and the peoples with his truth.
The LORD reigns! Let the whole earth celebrate! Let all the islands be glad!
Clouds and darkness surround him. Righteousness and justice hold up his throne.
Fire goes ahead of him and burns up his enemies on every side.
His lightning lights up the world. The earth sees it and shakes.
Mountains melt like wax before the LORD, before the Lord of the whole earth.
The skies tell of his righteousness. Every people has seen his glory.
Let everyone who serves carved images and brags about their idols be put to shame. Worship him, all you gods!
Zion heard and celebrated. The daughters of Judah rejoiced because of your judgments, LORD.
LORD, you are Most High over all the earth. You stand far above every god.
If you love the LORD, hate evil! He guards the lives of his faithful people and pulls them out of the grip of the wicked.
Light is planted for those who do right, and joy for those with honest hearts.
Rejoice in the LORD, you righteous people! Give thanks to his holy name.
A psalm. Sing the LORD a new song! He’s done wonders. His own right hand and holy arm won the victory.
The LORD has let everyone see how he saves. He’s shown his righteousness in plain sight of the nations.
He remembered his faithful love and loyalty to the house of Israel. People at the ends of the earth have seen our God save.
Shout for joy to the LORD, all the earth! Let the praise burst out in song!
Sing praises to the LORD with the harp. Let the harp and your voices make music together.
With trumpets and the blast of the ram’s horn, shout for joy before the King, the LORD.
Let the sea roar with everything in it. Let the world roar with everyone who lives in it.
Let the rivers clap their hands! Let the mountains sing for joy together.
Let them sing before the LORD, because he’s coming to judge the earth. He’ll judge the world with righteousness and treat the peoples fairly.
The LORD reigns! Let the peoples tremble. He sits on his throne among the cherubim. Let the earth shake.
The LORD is great in Zion. He stands high above every people.
Let them praise your great name, the name that fills them with awe. He is holy!
The mighty King loves justice. You make things fair. You do what’s just and right in Jacob.
Lift up the LORD our God. Bow down at his footstool. He is holy!
Moses and Aaron served among his priests, and Samuel was among those who called on his name. They called to the LORD, and he answered them.
He spoke to them from the pillar of cloud. They kept his teachings and the law he gave them.
You answered them, LORD our God. You forgave them, even as you held them accountable for what they did.
Lift up the LORD our God. Worship at his holy hill, because the LORD our God is holy!
A psalm of thanks. Shout for joy to the LORD, everyone on earth!
Serve the LORD with joy. Come into his presence singing!
Know that the LORD is God. He made us, and we belong to him. We’re his people, the sheep he looks after.
Walk through his gates giving thanks. Come into his courts with praise. Thank him and bless his name.
The LORD is good. His faithful love lasts forever, and he stays faithful through every generation.
A psalm by David. I’ll sing about faithful love and justice. LORD, you’re the one I’ll praise.
I’ll pay attention to how I live so I can walk with integrity. When will you come to me? Even in my own house, I’ll live with a heart that’s right.
I won’t set anything vile in front of my eyes. I hate what faithless people do. I won’t let any of it stick to me.
I’ll keep a twisted heart far from me. I’ll have nothing to do with evil.
If someone secretly runs down their neighbor, I’ll silence them. I won’t put up with people who look down on others and think too highly of themselves.
I’ll look for faithful people in the land and bring them to live with me. Those who walk with integrity will serve me.
Anyone who makes a habit of deceiving people won’t live under my roof. Liars won’t get to stay in my presence.
Morning after morning I’ll bring down every wicked person in the land, cutting off everyone who does evil from the LORD’s city.
A prayer for someone who’s suffering, worn down, and pouring out their trouble before the LORD. Hear my prayer, LORD! Let my cry reach you.
Don’t hide your face when trouble hits me. Lean in and listen. When I call, answer quickly.
My days disappear like smoke. My bones burn like a torch.
My heart has dried up like grass in the heat. I even forget to eat.
I groan so much that I’m nothing but skin and bones.
I’m like a pelican out in the wilderness, like an owl in a ruined place.
I lie awake, like a sparrow all alone on the roof.
My enemies insult me all day. Those who rage against me turn my name into a curse.
I eat ashes like bread and mix my drink with tears
because of your fierce anger. You picked me up and threw me aside.
My days are like a shadow stretching long. I’ve dried up like grass.
But you, LORD, will be here forever. Every generation will know your name.
You’ll rise and have mercy on Zion. It’s time to show her compassion. The time you set has come.
Your servants love her stones. Even her dust moves them to pity.
The nations will fear the LORD’s name, and every king on earth will stand in awe of your glory.
The LORD has rebuilt Zion and shown up in his glory.
He answered the prayer of people who had nothing. He didn’t brush off their prayer.
Write this down for the next generation, so a people yet to be created will praise the LORD.
He looked down from his sanctuary high above. From heaven the LORD looked at the earth
to hear prisoners groaning and set free those sentenced to death,
so people would tell of the LORD’s name in Zion and sing his praise in Jerusalem,
when peoples and kingdoms gather together to serve the LORD.
He drained my strength along the way. He cut my days short.
I said, “My God, don’t take me away halfway through my life. Your years stretch across every generation.
Long ago you laid the earth’s foundation. The heavens are your handiwork.
They’ll perish, but you’ll still be here. They’ll all wear out like clothes. You’ll change them like a coat, and they’ll be changed.
But you stay the same. Your years never end.
Your servants’ children will live on, and their descendants will stand secure before you.”
By David. Praise the LORD, my soul! Everything in me, praise his holy name!
Praise the LORD, my soul. Don’t forget a single good thing he’s done for you.
He forgives every sin and heals every disease.
He buys your life back from ruin and crowns you with faithful love and tender mercy.
He fills your life with good things so your youth comes back like an eagle’s.
The LORD does what’s right and brings justice to everyone who’s oppressed.
He showed Moses how he works and let the people of Israel see what he did.
The LORD is full of mercy and grace. He’s slow to anger and overflowing with faithful love.
He won’t keep accusing us or hold on to his anger forever.
He hasn’t treated us as our sins deserve or paid us back for what we’ve done wrong.
As high as the heavens are above the earth, that’s how great his faithful love is for those who fear him.
As far as east is from west, that’s how far he’s taken our wrongs away from us.
Like a father who feels for his children, the LORD has compassion on those who fear him.
He knows how we’re made. He remembers we’re dust.
Our days are like grass. We bloom like flowers in a field.
The wind blows over a flower and it’s gone. Even the spot where it grew forgets it.
But the LORD’s faithful love goes from forever to forever for those who fear him. His righteousness reaches their children’s children,
those who keep his covenant and remember to follow his instructions.
The LORD set up his throne in heaven, and his kingdom rules over everything.
Praise the LORD, you mighty angels who carry out what he says and obey his voice.
Praise the LORD, all his armies, all you servants who do what pleases him.
Praise the LORD, everything he’s made, everywhere he rules. Praise the LORD, my soul!
Bless the LORD, my soul! LORD my God, you are so great. You wear honor and majesty like a robe.
You wrap yourself in light like a garment and stretch out the heavens like a curtain.
You set the beams of your rooms in the waters. You ride the clouds like a chariot and walk on the wings of the wind.
You make winds your messengers and flames of fire your servants.
You laid the earth on its foundations so it would never be moved.
You wrapped it in deep water like a cloak. The waters stood higher than the mountains.
At your rebuke they ran. At the sound of your thunder they rushed away.
The mountains rose and the valleys sank into the places you set for them.
You drew a line the waters can’t cross, so they’ll never come back to cover the earth.
You send springs into the valleys, and they run between the mountains.
Every animal in the fields drinks from them. Wild donkeys come and quench their thirst.
Birds nest beside the streams and sing from the branches.
From your rooms above, you water the mountains. The earth is filled with the fruit of what you do.
You grow grass for livestock and plants for people to tend, so they can bring food out of the ground:
wine to lift their hearts, oil to make their faces shine, and bread to give them strength.
The LORD’s trees drink their fill, the cedars of Lebanon that he planted.
Birds build their nests there. The stork makes its home in the cypresses.
The high mountains are home to wild goats. The rocks shelter the rock badgers.
You set the moon to mark the seasons. The sun knows when it’s time to go down.
You bring on the dark, and night comes. Then all the forest animals come out and prowl.
Young lions roar for prey and look to God for their food.
When the sun comes up, they slip away and lie down in their dens.
Then people go out to work and keep at it until evening.
LORD, look how much you’ve made! You made it all with wisdom. The earth is full of your riches.
There’s the sea, huge and wide, full of creatures too many to count, from the smallest to the largest.
Ships sail there, and Leviathan is there too, the creature you made to play in the sea.
They all look to you to give them food when it’s time.
You give it, and they gather it up. You open your hand, and they have their fill of good things.
When you hide your face, they’re terrified. When you take their breath away, they die and go back to dust.
You send out your Spirit, and they come to life. You make the face of the earth new again.
May the LORD’s glory last forever. May the LORD take joy in what he’s made.
He looks at the earth and it shakes. He touches the mountains and they smoke.
I’ll sing to the LORD as long as I live. I’ll praise my God as long as I’m here.
May what I think about please him. I’ll take joy in the LORD.
Let sinners be swept off the earth. Let the wicked be gone. Bless the LORD, my soul. Praise the LORD!
Give thanks to the LORD! Call on his name. Let every people know what he’s done.
Sing to him! Sing his praises and tell about every wonder he’s worked.
Take pride in his holy name. Let the hearts of everyone looking for the LORD fill with joy.
Look to the LORD and his strength. Keep seeking his face.
Remember the amazing things he’s done, the wonders he worked and the judgments he spoke,
you descendants of his servant Abraham, you children of Jacob whom he chose.
He’s the LORD our God. His judgments reach across the whole earth.
He remembers his covenant forever, the word he commanded for a thousand generations.
It’s the covenant he made with Abraham and the oath he swore to Isaac.
He confirmed it to Jacob as a law, to Israel as a covenant that lasts forever.
He said, “I’ll give you the land of Canaan. That’s the share you’ll inherit.”
He said it when they were only a handful of people, strangers in the land.
They moved from nation to nation, from one kingdom to another people.
He let no one mistreat them. He even called out kings for their sake:
“Keep your hands off my anointed ones! Don’t do a thing to harm my prophets!”
He called down famine on the land and cut off their food supply.
He sent someone ahead of them. Joseph was sold as a slave.
Shackles bruised his feet, and an iron collar locked around his neck,
until what he’d said came true and the LORD’s word proved him right.
The king, a ruler over peoples, sent for him and set him free.
He put Joseph in charge of his household and everything he owned,
with authority to discipline his officials as he saw fit and teach his elders wisdom.
Then Israel came to Egypt, and Jacob made his home in the land of Ham.
God made his people grow in number until they were stronger than their enemies.
He turned the Egyptians’ hearts against his people, and they plotted against his servants.
He sent Moses, his servant, and Aaron, the man he had chosen.
They worked miracles in front of the people and did wonders in the land of Ham.
He sent darkness, and the land went dark. They didn’t rebel against his words.
He turned their water to blood and killed their fish.
Frogs swarmed over the land and got into the rooms of their kings.
He spoke, and swarms of flies came, with lice all across their land.
He sent hail instead of rain, and lightning flashed through their land.
He struck their vines and fig trees and shattered the trees across the country.
He spoke, and locusts and grasshoppers came in numbers no one could count.
They ate every plant in the land and devoured everything the ground produced.
He struck down all the firstborn in the land, the first fruits of their strength.
He led his people out with silver and gold, and no one among his tribes was too weak to keep up.
Egypt was glad to see them leave, because the people were terrified of them.
He spread a cloud over them for shelter and gave them fire to light up the night.
They asked for food, so he brought them quail and filled them with bread from the sky.
He opened the rock, and water gushed out. It ran like a river through the dry ground.
He remembered his holy promise and his servant Abraham.
He brought his people out rejoicing. The ones he chose came out singing.
He gave them the lands of the nations, and they took possession of what those peoples had worked for,
so they could keep his statutes and follow his laws. Praise the LORD!
Praise the LORD! Thank the LORD because he’s good. His faithful love lasts forever.
Who could tell everything the LORD has done in his power? Who could give him all the praise he deserves?
Blessed are those who stand up for justice and do what’s right every time.
Remember me, LORD, when you show favor to your people. Come save me too,
so I can see the people you chose thrive, share your nation’s joy, and celebrate with those who belong to you.
We’ve sinned just like our ancestors. We’ve done wrong. We’ve acted wickedly.
Our ancestors missed what your wonders in Egypt meant. They forgot how often you’d shown them faithful love. They rebelled right there at the Red Sea.
Even so, he saved them for the sake of his name, to show just how strong he is.
He rebuked the Red Sea, and it dried up. He led them through the depths as if they were walking through a desert.
He saved them from the grip of those who hated them and bought them back from the enemy’s hand.
The waters covered their enemies. Nobody was left.
Then they believed his words and sang his praise.
But they forgot what he’d done almost immediately. They didn’t wait for his advice.
They let their cravings take over in the desert and put God to the test in the wasteland.
He gave them what they asked for, but left them wasting away inside.
In the camp they grew jealous of Moses and of Aaron, the LORD’s holy one.
The ground opened and swallowed Dathan and buried Abiram’s group.
A fire broke out among them and burned up the wicked.
At Horeb they made a calf and bowed down to a statue cast from metal.
They traded their glory for a statue of a bull that eats grass.
They forgot God, the one who’d saved them and done great things in Egypt,
wonders in the land of Ham and things that filled people with awe at the Red Sea.
He said he would destroy them, but Moses, the one he chose, stepped into the breach before him and turned his wrath away so he wouldn’t wipe them out.
