What will you get for this? What else is coming to you, you lying tongue?
Sharp arrows from a warrior, along with burning juniper coals.
What misery, living as a stranger in Meshech, staying among the tents of Kedar!
I’ve lived way too long with people who hate peace.
I’m for peace, but the moment I speak, they’re ready for war.
A song of ascents. I lift my eyes to the hills. Where’s my help coming from?
My help comes from the LORD, the one who made heaven and earth.
He won’t let your foot slip. The one who watches over you won’t doze off.
Look, the one who watches over Israel never dozes and never sleeps.
The LORD watches over you. He’s the shade right beside you.
The sun won’t harm you by day, and the moon won’t harm you by night.
The LORD will guard you from every evil. He’ll watch over your life.
The LORD will watch over you when you go out and when you come home, from now on and forever.
A song of ascents. By David. I was so glad when they said to me, “Let’s go to the LORD’s house!”
And here we are, Jerusalem, standing inside your gates!
Jerusalem is built like a city held tightly together.
The tribes go up there, the LORD’s own tribes, to thank the LORD by name, just as Israel was told.
That’s where the thrones for judgment stand, the thrones of David’s family.
Pray for Jerusalem’s peace. May everyone who loves you thrive.
May there be peace inside your walls and well-being in your palaces.
For my family and friends, I’ll say, “May peace be within you.”
For the sake of the house of the LORD our God, I’ll work for your good.
A song of ascents. I lift my eyes to you, the one who sits in heaven.
As servants watch their master’s hand, as a servant girl watches her mistress’s hand, we keep our eyes on the LORD our God until he shows us mercy.
Have mercy on us, LORD. Have mercy on us. We’ve taken more than enough contempt.
We’ve had our fill of insults from people who have it easy and of contempt from the proud.
A song of ascents. By David. If the LORD hadn’t been on our side, let Israel say it now,
if the LORD hadn’t been on our side when people rose against us,
they would’ve swallowed us alive when their anger flared up at us.
The flood would’ve swept us away. The current would’ve gone right over us.
Those raging waters would’ve swallowed us up.
Blessed be the LORD, who didn’t leave us for their teeth to tear apart.
We got out like a bird escaping a hunter’s trap. The trap broke, and we got away.
Our help is in the name of the LORD, who made heaven and earth.
A song of ascents. People who trust the LORD are like Mount Zion. It can’t be shaken. It stands forever.
Just as mountains surround Jerusalem, the LORD surrounds his people from now on and forever.
The scepter of the wicked won’t stay over the land given to the righteous, so the righteous won’t turn their own hands to evil.
LORD, do good to people who do good, to those whose hearts are upright.
But the people who turn off onto crooked paths, the LORD will lead away with those who do evil. Peace be on Israel.
A song of ascents. When the LORD brought us back to Zion, it felt like we were dreaming.
We couldn’t stop laughing and singing. Even the nations said, “The LORD has done great things for them.”
The LORD really has done great things for us, and we’re full of joy.
Restore our fortunes again, LORD, like streams flowing through the Negev.
Those who plant in tears will harvest with shouts of joy.
The one who goes out crying with seed to sow will come back singing for joy, carrying armfuls of grain.
A song of ascents. By Solomon. Unless the LORD builds the house, the builders work for nothing. Unless the LORD watches the city, the guard stays up for nothing.
Getting up early, staying up late, and working yourself ragged just to eat won’t get you anywhere. The LORD gives sleep to the people he loves.
Look, children are an inheritance from the LORD. The fruit of the womb is his reward.
Children born when you’re young are like arrows in a warrior’s hand.
Happy is the one whose quiver is full of them. They won’t be put to shame when they face their enemies at the city gate.
A song of ascents. Blessed is everyone who fears the LORD and walks in his ways.
You’ll eat what you’ve worked for with your own hands. You’ll be glad, and life will go well for you.
Your wife will be like a vine loaded with fruit within your home. Your children will be like young olive shoots around your table.
That’s how the LORD blesses the one who fears him.
May the LORD bless you from Zion. May you see Jerusalem thrive every day of your life.
May you live to see your grandchildren. Peace be on Israel.
A song of ascents. They’ve caused me pain over and over since I was young. Let Israel say it now:
They’ve caused me pain over and over since I was young, but they haven’t beaten me.
They plowed across my back, cutting long furrows.
The LORD does what’s right. He cut the ropes of the wicked.
Let everyone who hates Zion be put to shame and turned back.
Let them be like grass on a roof, drying up before it has a chance to grow.
Nobody harvesting gets even a handful of it. Nobody tying bundles gets an armful.
People walking past don’t say, “The LORD bless you. We bless you in the LORD’s name.”
A song of ascents. From down in the depths I cry out to you, LORD.
Lord, hear my voice. Listen closely when I beg for help.
LORD, if you kept track of every sin, who could stand before you?
But you forgive, and that’s why we stand in awe of you.
I’m waiting for the LORD with my whole soul. I put my hope in what he says.
I long for the Lord more than guards long for morning, more than guards long for morning.
Israel, put your hope in the LORD. Faithful love is with him, and he has more than enough power to redeem.
He’ll redeem Israel from all their sins.
A song of ascents. By David. LORD, my heart isn’t proud, and I don’t look down on people. I don’t get wrapped up in big matters or things too wonderful for me.
I’ve settled my soul and quieted it. Like a weaned child resting with its mother, my soul is quiet inside me.
Israel, put your hope in the LORD, from now on and forever.
A song of ascents. LORD, remember David and everything he went through.
Remember how he swore to the LORD and made a promise to the Mighty One of Jacob:
“I won’t step inside my house or climb into my bed.
I won’t close my eyes and sleep or even let myself doze
until I find a place for the LORD, a home for the Mighty One of Jacob.”
We heard about it in Ephrathah and found it in the field of Jaar.
“Let’s go to his home. Let’s bow down and worship at his footstool.”
Rise up, LORD, and come to your resting place, you and the ark of your strength.
Dress your priests in righteousness, and let your faithful people shout for joy!
For the sake of your servant David, don’t turn your anointed one away.
The LORD gave David his word, and he’ll keep it: “I’ll put one of your own descendants on your throne.
If your children keep my covenant and the teaching I give them, their children will sit on your throne forever.”
The LORD chose Zion. That’s where he wanted to make his home.
“This is my resting place forever. I’ll live here because this is where I want to be.
I’ll bless it with plenty of food. I’ll give its poor enough bread to eat their fill.
I’ll dress its priests in salvation, and its faithful people will shout for joy.
There I’ll make David’s horn sprout. I’ve set a lamp in place for my anointed one.
I’ll dress his enemies in shame, and his own crown will shine.”
A song of ascents. By David. Look how good it is, how beautiful, when brothers live together in peace!
It’s like precious oil poured on the head, running down the beard, down Aaron’s beard, all the way to the edge of his robes.
It’s like dew from Hermon falling on Zion’s hills. That’s where the LORD gives his blessing: life forever.
A song of ascents. Come on, praise the LORD, all you servants who stand in his house through the night!
Lift your hands in the sanctuary and praise the LORD!
May the LORD, who made heaven and earth, bless you from Zion.
Praise the LORD! Praise his name! Praise him, all you who serve the LORD,
you who stand in the LORD’s house, in the courts of our God’s house.
Praise the LORD, because he’s good. Sing praise to his name, because it’s a joy to do it.
The LORD chose Jacob for himself. He made Israel his own.
I know the LORD is great. Our Lord is above every god.
The LORD does whatever he wants, in heaven and on earth, in the seas and in the deepest waters.
He brings clouds up from the ends of the earth, sends lightning with the rain, and lets the wind out of his storehouses.
He struck down Egypt’s firstborn, both people and animals.
He sent signs and wonders right into the middle of Egypt, against Pharaoh and all his servants.
He struck down many nations and killed powerful kings,
Sihon king of the Amorites, Og king of Bashan, and all the kingdoms of Canaan.
He gave their land as an inheritance to Israel, his own people.
Your name lasts forever, LORD. Every generation will know what you’ve done.
The LORD will judge his people and have compassion on his servants.
The nations’ idols are silver and gold, made by human hands.
They have mouths that can’t speak and eyes that can’t see.
They have ears that can’t hear, and there’s no breath in their mouths.
Those who make them will end up like them, and so will everyone who trusts them.
Family of Israel, praise the LORD! Family of Aaron, praise the LORD!
Family of Levi, praise the LORD! Everyone who fears the LORD, praise him!
Blessed be the LORD from Zion, the one who lives in Jerusalem. Praise the LORD!
Thank the LORD because he’s good. His faithful love lasts forever.
Thank the God of gods. His faithful love lasts forever.
Thank the Lord of lords. His faithful love lasts forever.
the one who alone does great wonders. His faithful love lasts forever.
who made the heavens with understanding. His faithful love lasts forever.
who spread the earth out above the waters. His faithful love lasts forever.
who made the great lights. His faithful love lasts forever.
the sun to rule the day. His faithful love lasts forever.
the moon and stars to rule the night. His faithful love lasts forever.
who struck down Egypt’s firstborn. His faithful love lasts forever.
and brought Israel out from among the Egyptians. His faithful love lasts forever.
with a strong hand and an arm stretched out. His faithful love lasts forever.
who split the Red Sea in two. His faithful love lasts forever.
and led Israel right through the middle. His faithful love lasts forever.
but swept Pharaoh and his army away in the Red Sea. His faithful love lasts forever.
who led his people through the wilderness. His faithful love lasts forever.
who brought down great kings. His faithful love lasts forever.
and killed mighty kings. His faithful love lasts forever.
Sihon, king of the Amorites. His faithful love lasts forever.
and Og, king of Bashan. His faithful love lasts forever.
who gave their land as an inheritance. His faithful love lasts forever.
an inheritance for Israel, his servant. His faithful love lasts forever.
who remembered us when we were brought low. His faithful love lasts forever.
and rescued us from our enemies. His faithful love lasts forever.
who feeds every living creature. His faithful love lasts forever.
Thank the God of heaven. His faithful love lasts forever.
We sat by the rivers of Babylon and cried when Zion came to mind.
We hung our harps on the willows there.
The people who took us captive asked for songs. The ones who tormented us wanted us to sound happy: “Sing us one of Zion’s songs!”
How are we supposed to sing the LORD’s song in a foreign land?
Jerusalem, if I forget you, let my right hand forget how to play.
Let my tongue stick to the roof of my mouth if I forget you, if I don’t hold Jerusalem above my greatest joy.
LORD, remember what Edom’s people did the day Jerusalem fell. They shouted, “Tear it down! Tear it down to the foundations!”
Daughter of Babylon, you’re headed for ruin. Happy is the one who pays you back for what you did to us.
Happy is the one who takes your little ones and dashes them against the rock.
By David. I’ll thank you with all my heart. Right in front of the gods, I’ll sing your praise.
I’ll bow toward your holy temple and thank you for your name, your faithful love, and your truth. You’ve lifted your name and your word above everything.
The day I called, you answered. You gave me fresh courage and strength deep inside.
Every king on earth will thank you, LORD, because they’ve heard what you said.
They’ll sing about your ways, LORD, because your glory is so great!
Even though the LORD is high above us, he looks after people who are lowly. He recognizes the proud from far away.
Even when I’m walking right through trouble, you keep me alive. You reach out against my enemies’ rage, and your right hand saves me.
The LORD will finish what concerns me. Your faithful love lasts forever, LORD. Don’t walk away from what your own hands have made.
For the music director. A psalm by David. LORD, you’ve searched me through and through. You know me.
You know when I sit and when I get up. You catch my thoughts from far away.
You see where I go and where I lie down. You know every move I make.
Before a word even reaches my tongue, LORD, you already know the whole thing.
You surround me, behind and ahead, and rest your hand on me.
That kind of knowledge is beyond me. It’s too high for me to reach.
Where could I go to get away from your Spirit? Where could I run from your presence?
If I climb into heaven, you’re there. If I make my bed in Sheol, look, you’re there too!
If I ride on the wings of dawn and settle at the far edge of the sea,
even there your hand will guide me, and your right hand will hold on to me.
If I say, “The dark will swallow me up for sure. The light around me will turn to night,”
even darkness can’t hide anything from you. Night shines like day. Darkness and light are the same to you.
You shaped the deepest parts of me. You knit me together in my mother’s womb.
I thank you because the way you made me fills me with awe and wonder. What you make is wonderful. Deep down, I know it.
You saw my frame when I was made in secret, woven together in the depths of the earth.
You saw my body before it was finished. Every day you’d planned for me was written in your book before a single one had begun.
God, your thoughts are precious to me! There are so many of them.
If I tried to count them, there’d be more than grains of sand. When I wake up, I’m still with you.
God, if only you’d do away with the wicked! Get away from me, you bloodthirsty people!
They speak against you with evil intent. Your enemies use your name as if it means nothing.
LORD, don’t I hate the ones who hate you? Doesn’t it grieve me when people rise against you?
I hate them completely. They’ve made themselves my enemies.
Search me, God, and know my heart. Put me to the test and know my thoughts.
See if there’s any evil path in me, and lead me in the way that lasts forever.
For the music director. A psalm by David. Rescue me from evil people, LORD. Keep me safe from violent people.
They’re planning harm deep down. They keep getting together to make war.
They sharpen their tongues like snakes. There’s viper venom under their lips. Selah.
LORD, keep me out of the grip of the wicked. Protect me from violent people set on tripping me up.
Proud people have hidden a trap for me. They’ve stretched a net by the path and laid snares for me. Selah.
I said to the LORD, “You’re my God.” LORD, listen when I cry for help.
LORD, my Lord, you’re the strength that saves me. You covered my head when battle came.
LORD, don’t give the wicked what they want. Don’t let their plans work, or they’ll get even prouder. Selah.
As for the people surrounding me, let the trouble they spoke come down on their own heads.
Let burning coals fall on them. Let them be thrown into fire, into muddy pits they’ll never climb out of.
People who speak evil won’t get a foothold in the land. Let trouble hunt down the violent and bring them down.
I know the LORD will stand up for people who are suffering and see that the needy get justice.
The righteous will thank you for your name. The upright will live in your presence.
A psalm by David. LORD, I’m calling to you. Come quickly! Listen to my voice when I call.
Let my prayer rise before you like incense. Let my raised hands be like the evening sacrifice.
Set a guard over my mouth, LORD. Keep watch at the door of my lips.
Keep my heart from leaning toward evil or joining in with people who do wrong. Don’t let me share their rich food.
If someone who lives rightly strikes me, let me take it as kindness. Their correction is like oil on my head. Let me accept it. I’ll keep praying against evil deeds.
When their judges are thrown down the sides of the cliff, they’ll hear my words and know they were well spoken.
“Like soil broken up by a plow, our bones are scattered at the mouth of Sheol.”
My eyes are on you, LORD, my Lord. I take refuge in you. Don’t leave my soul with nothing.
Keep me out of the snare they’ve set for me, out of the traps of people who do evil.
Let the wicked fall together into their own nets while I walk safely past.
A psalm for reflection by David, when he was in the cave. A prayer. I cry out loud to the LORD. I lift my voice and beg him for mercy.
I pour out my complaint in front of him. I tell him exactly what’s hurting me.
When my spirit felt crushed, you knew the way I was taking. On the path I walk, they’ve hidden a trap for me.
Look to my right and see. Nobody’s looking out for me. I have nowhere to run, and nobody cares whether I live.
I cried out to you, LORD. I said, “You’re my refuge, my share in the land of the living.”
Listen to my cry, because I’m desperate. Save me from the people chasing me. They’re too strong for me.
Get me out of this prison so I can thank you for your name. The righteous will gather around me because you’ll be good to me.
A psalm by David. Hear my prayer, LORD. Listen to what I’m asking. In your faithfulness and righteousness, come to my aid.
Don’t bring your servant to trial. Nobody alive is righteous in your sight.
The enemy is after my life. He’s crushed me into the ground and made me live in dark places like people long dead.
My spirit caves in under it all. Inside, my heart feels empty.
I remember the old days. I think about everything you’ve done and turn over in my mind what your hands have made.
I stretch my hands out to you. My soul thirsts for you like land cracked and dry. Selah.
Answer me quickly, LORD. My spirit is giving out. Don’t hide your face from me or I’ll be like those going down to the pit.
Let me hear of your faithful love in the morning, because I trust you. Show me the way I should go. I lift my soul up to you.
Rescue me from my enemies, LORD. I’m running to you for shelter.
Teach me to do what you want, because you’re my God. Your Spirit is good. Lead me on upright ground.
Bring me back to life, LORD, for the sake of your name. In your righteousness, pull me out of trouble.
In your faithful love, cut off my enemies and put an end to everyone who comes after my life, because I’m your servant.
A psalm by David. Praise the LORD, my rock! He trains my hands for war and gets my fingers ready for battle.
He's the one who loves me, my fortress, my lookout tower, my rescuer and my shield. He's where I run for safety, and he brings my people under my rule.
LORD, what are we humans that you'd care about us? Who are we that you'd even think of us?
We're like a breath. Our days slip by like a passing shadow.
Open up the heavens, LORD, and come down. Touch the mountains and watch them smoke.
Flash your lightning and scatter them. Fire your arrows and send them running.
Reach down from above and pull me out. Get me out of these deep waters, out of the hands of foreigners.
They lie through their teeth, and even the hand they raise to swear an oath can't be trusted.
God, I've got a new song for you. I'll play my ten-string lyre and sing your praises. 🎶
You're the one who saves kings. You pull your servant David clear of the sword that could kill him.
Get me out of the hands of foreigners. They lie through their teeth, and even the hand they raise to swear an oath can't be trusted.
Then our sons will stand like plants that have grown up strong, and our daughters like pillars carved to make a palace beautiful.
Our barns will be packed with supplies of every kind. Our sheep will multiply by the thousands and tens of thousands out in our fields.
Our oxen will haul heavy loads. No one will break in, no one will be driven away, and no cries of distress will ring through our streets.
Happy are the people who get to live like that! Happy are the people whose God is the LORD!
A praise song by David. My God, my King, I'll lift you high. I'll praise your name forever and ever.
Every single day I'll praise you. I'll speak your name with praise forever and ever.
The LORD is great and deserves all the praise! No one can get to the bottom of how great he is.
One generation will tell the next what you've done, passing on the stories of your mighty acts.
I'll take time to think about your glory and majesty and all the amazing things you've done.
People will talk about the sheer power of the things you've done. I'll tell them how great you are.
They'll tell the stories of how good you've been, and they'll sing about how you always do what's right.
The LORD is gracious and full of mercy. He's slow to get angry and overflowing with faithful love.
The LORD is good to everyone. His tender mercy reaches everything he's made.
Everything you've made will thank you, LORD. Your faithful people will praise you.
They'll talk about the glory of your kingdom and tell each other about your power,
so people everywhere can hear what mighty things you've done and how glorious and majestic your kingdom is.
Your kingdom lasts forever. You rule through every generation. The LORD keeps every word he gives and shows love in everything he does.
The LORD catches everyone who's falling and lifts up everyone who's bent low.
Every eye looks to you, waiting. You give them their food right when it's time.
You open your hand and give every living thing what it longs for.
The LORD is right in all his ways and gracious in everything he does.
The LORD is close to everyone who calls on him, everyone who calls on him sincerely.
He gives those who honor him what they long for. He hears them cry for help and saves them.
The LORD keeps everyone who loves him safe, but he'll destroy all the wicked.
I'll keep speaking the LORD's praise. Let every living creature bless his holy name forever and ever.
Praise the LORD! Come on, my soul, praise the LORD!
As long as I'm alive, I'll praise the LORD. As long as I'm here, I'll sing to my God.
Don't pin your hopes on rulers. They're human, and they can't save you.
When their spirit leaves, they go back to the dirt. That same day, all their plans disappear.
Happy are those who have the God of Jacob on their side, who put their hope in the LORD their God.
He made heaven and earth, the sea and everything in them. He stays faithful forever.
He makes sure the oppressed get justice and the hungry get food. The LORD sets prisoners free.
The LORD opens the eyes of the blind. He lifts up those bent low. The LORD loves those who do right.
The LORD looks after foreigners. He supports children without fathers and women who've lost their husbands, but he turns the plans of the wicked upside down.
The LORD will reign forever. Zion, your God will rule through every generation. Praise the LORD!
Praise the LORD! Singing to our God feels good, and he's worth every bit of praise.
The LORD builds Jerusalem back up. He brings home the people Israel lost to exile.
He heals broken hearts and wraps up their wounds.
He counts every star and calls each one by name.
Our Lord is great, and his power is huge. There's no limit to what he understands.
The LORD holds up the humble and brings the wicked down to the dirt.
Sing to the LORD and thank him. Play the harp and sing to our God,
the one who fills the sky with clouds, gets rain ready for the earth, and makes grass grow on the mountains.
He feeds the livestock and the baby ravens when they cry out.
A horse's strength doesn't impress him. A man's powerful legs don't thrill him either.
The LORD delights in those who honor him with awe, those who put their hope in his faithful love.
Jerusalem, praise the LORD! Zion, praise your God!
He's made the bars on your gates strong and blessed the children who live inside.
He gives you peace all the way to your borders and feeds you with the finest wheat.
He sends his command out across the earth, and his word moves fast.
He lays down snow like wool and sprinkles frost like ashes.
He flings down hail like little stones. Who can stand up to that cold?
Then he gives the word, and it all melts. He sends his wind blowing, and the waters start to flow.
He gives his word to Jacob and makes his laws and rulings known to Israel.
He hasn't done this for any other nation. They don't know his rulings. Praise the LORD!
Praise the LORD! Praise him from the heavens! Praise him way up high!
Praise him, all his angels! Praise him, all his armies!
Praise him, sun and moon! Every shining star, praise him!
Praise him, highest heavens, and you waters above the skies!
Let them praise the LORD's name. He spoke the command, and there they were.
He set them in place forever and ever. The order he gave will never expire.
Praise the LORD from the earth, you giant sea creatures and all you ocean depths!
Lightning and hail, snow and clouds, storm winds that do what he says,
mountains and hills, fruit trees and every cedar,
wild animals and livestock, little creatures and birds on the wing,
kings of the earth and people everywhere, rulers and all the judges on earth,
young men and young women, old men and children too.
Let them all praise the LORD's name. His name alone is lifted high. His glory rises over earth and heaven.
He's lifted up his people's strength and given his faithful ones reason to praise. That's Israel, the people he holds close. Praise the LORD!
Praise the LORD! Sing him a new song. When his faithful people get together, fill the room with his praise.
Israel, celebrate the one who made you. People of Zion, take joy in your King!
Praise his name with dancing! Grab the tambourine and harp and sing to him!
The LORD takes joy in his people. He crowns the humble by saving them.
Let his faithful people celebrate the honor he gives them. Let them sing for joy even on their beds.
Let God's highest praises be on their lips and a double-edged sword in their hands,
to carry out vengeance on the nations and bring punishment on the peoples,
to put their kings in chains and their nobles in iron shackles,
and to carry out the judgment written against them. This honor belongs to all his faithful people. Praise the LORD!
Praise the LORD! Praise God in his holy place! Praise him in his mighty heavens!
Praise him for the powerful things he's done! Give him praise as great as he is!
Blast the trumpet to praise him! Praise him with harp and lyre!
Praise him with a tambourine and some dancing! Bring the strings and the flute and praise him!
Crash those cymbals in praise! Let the cymbals ring out for him!
If you've got breath, praise the LORD! Praise the LORD!
